words.en: If you appeal to someone to do something, you make a serious and urgent request to them. If you appeal against a decision or sentence, you formally ask a court or other authority to change it. If something appeals to you, you like it or it interests you.

words.tr: adj. 引起兴趣的； v. 吸引；“appeal”的现在分词；
words.ex: The book has an appealing story.
words.ex_cn: 这本书有一个引人入胜的故事。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as appealing, you mean that you like them or they make you want to have or do something.

words.ex: The sun appears in the sky at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在黎明时出现。
words.en: If someone or something appears, they come into sight or become noticeable.

words.tr: n. 外观；外表；出现；露面；
words.ex: The appearance of the house surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子的外观让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The way that someone or something looks or the act of coming into view.

words.ex: The appendix contains extra data for the report.
words.ex_cn: 附录包含了报告的额外数据。
words.en: An appendix is a section at the end of a book that contains additional information. It can also refer to the small tube attached to the large intestine in the human body, known as the vermiform appendix.

words.ex: He has an appetite for spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢辛辣食物。
words.en: A desire or liking for something, especially food.

words.ex: The crowd applauded after the performance.
words.ex_cn: 演出结束后，观众鼓掌了。
words.en: To applaud means to show approval or praise by clapping the hands.

words.ex: The audience gave applause after the song.
words.ex_cn: 歌曲结束后，观众鼓掌了。
words.en: Applause is the noise made by a group of people clapping their hands to show approval or enjoyment.

words.ex: He eats an apple every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃一个苹果。
words.en: A round fruit with firm, white flesh and a green, red, or yellow skin.

words.ex: The kitchen has a new washing appliance.
words.ex_cn: 厨房里有一台新的洗衣机。
words.en: An appliance is a device or machine that is used to perform a particular task, especially in the home.

words.ex: This rule is applicable to all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: If something is applicable to a particular situation, it is relevant or suitable for that situation.

words.ex: The applicant filled out the form carefully.
words.ex_cn: 这位申请人仔细填写了表格。
words.en: An applicant is someone who applies for something, especially a job.

words.ex: He submitted his application for the job last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周提交了那份工作申请。
words.en: An application is a formal request, often written, for something such as a job, a place at a university, or permission to do something. It can also refer to the act of putting something to a special use or purpose, or a program or piece of software designed to perform a specific function.

words.ex: He wants to apply for a job at the bank.
words.ex_cn: 他想申请银行的工作。
words.en: To make a formal request, usually in writing, for something such as a job, a place at a university, or permission to do something.

words.ex: The boss appointed Tom as the new manager.
words.ex_cn: 老板任命汤姆为新经理。
words.en: If you appoint someone to a job or official position, you formally choose them for it.

words.ex: I have an appointment with my doctor at 3 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 我下午三点有个医生的约会。
words.en: An appointment is a formal arrangement to meet or visit someone at a particular time, especially for a purpose connected with their work or official position.

words.ex: The boss gave a positive appraisal of his work.
words.ex_cn: 老板对他的工作给予了积极的评估。
words.en: An appraisal is a judgement or assessment of the value, nature, or quality of something or someone.

words.ex: He apprized me of the changes in the schedule.
words.ex_cn: 他告知我日程的变化。
words.en: To inform or notify someone of something.

words.tr: adj. 可觉察的；很可观的
words.ex: There is an appreciable difference in his grades.
words.ex_cn: 他的成绩有明显的差异。
words.en: If something is appreciable, it is large enough to be noticed or considered important.

words.ex: The temperature rose appreciably after noon.
words.ex_cn: 中午过后，温度明显上升了。
words.en: To a noticeable or significant extent; considerably.

words.ex: I appreciate the beauty of nature.
words.ex_cn: 我欣赏大自然的美。
words.en: If you appreciate something, you recognize its value and feel grateful for it.

words.ex: He showed appreciation for her hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他对她的辛勤工作表示欣赏。
words.en: Recognition of the quality, value, significance, or magnitude of people and things.

words.tr: adj. 感激的；欣赏的；表示赞赏的
words.ex: She was appreciative of his help.
words.ex_cn: 她对他的帮助心怀感激。
words.en: If you are appreciative of something, you are grateful for it.

words.ex: He felt apprehension before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到焦虑。
words.en: Anxiety or fear that something bad or unpleasant will happen; understanding; the action of arresting someone.

words.ex: He is an apprentice in a car repair shop.
words.ex_cn: 他是汽车修理店的一名学徒。
words.en: An apprentice is a young person who works for someone in order to learn their skill.

words.tr:
n. 方法；接近；靠近；路径；
v. 接近；靠近；临近；处理；
words.ex: He used a new approach to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一种新方法来解决问题。
words.en: To come near or nearer to something or someone in distance or time.

words.tr: adj. 适当的；合适的；恰当的；
words.ex: This dress is appropriate for a wedding.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子适合参加婚礼。
words.en: Something that is appropriate is suitable or acceptable for a particular situation.

words.ex: The teacher gave her approval for the project.
words.ex_cn: 老师对这个项目表示了赞成。
words.en: If you give your approval to something, you agree with it or allow it to happen.

words.tr: v. 批准；认可；通过；赞成(连of)
words.ex: My mom will approve my new phone.
words.ex_cn: 我妈妈会同意我买新手机。
words.en: If you approve of an action, event, or suggestion, you like it or are pleased about it.

words.tr:
adj. 近似的；大约的；
v. 接近；
words.ex: The approximate cost is $50.
words.ex_cn: 费用大约是50美元。
words.en: An approximate number, time, or position is close to the correct number, time, or position, but is not exact.

words.ex: The trip takes approximately 30 minutes.
words.ex_cn: 这段旅程大约需要30分钟。
words.en: Used to indicate that something is close to the actual, but not completely accurate or exact.

words.ex: The approximation of pi is 3.14.
words.ex_cn: π的近似值是3.14。
words.en: An approximation is a fact, object, or description which is similar to something else, but which is not exactly the same.

words.ex: She was born in April.
words.ex_cn: 她出生于四月。
words.en: The fourth month of the year, in the northern hemisphere usually considered the second month of spring.

words.ex: His answer was apt for the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答对这个问题很恰当。
words.en: If someone is apt to do something, they often do it and so it is likely that they will do it again.

words.ex: He has a natural aptitude for math.
words.ex_cn: 他天生有数学天赋。
words.en: An aptitude is a natural ability to do something.

words.tr: n. 水族馆；水族箱；养鱼缸；
words.ex: We visited the aquarium to see the fish.
words.ex_cn: 我们去水族馆看鱼。
words.en: A tank or building in which fish and other water creatures and plants are kept.

words.tr: adj. 水生的；水栖的；水中的；
words.ex: The fish live in aquatic plants.
words.ex_cn: 这些鱼生活在水生植物中。
words.en: Relating to water; living in or near water or taking place in water.

words.tr:
adj. 阿拉伯的；阿拉伯人的；
n. 阿拉伯人；
words.ex: He ate arab food at the restaurant.
words.ex_cn: 他在餐厅吃了阿拉伯食物。
words.en: An Arab is a person whose native language is Arabic and who comes from or lives in the Arabic-speaking world.

words.ex: He wore an arabian robe to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着一件阿拉伯长袍去参加派对。
words.en: Of or relating to Arabia or its people, language, or culture.

words.tr:
n. 阿拉伯语；
adj. 阿拉伯（语）的；
words.ex: He speaks Arabic fluently.
words.ex_cn: 他流利地说阿拉伯语。
words.en: Relating to the Arabs or their language, culture, or civilization.

words.ex: The land is arable and good for growing wheat.
words.ex_cn: 这块地是可耕的，适合种植小麦。
words.en: Arable land is land that is suitable for growing crops.

words.ex: The teacher chose an arbitrary number to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 老师随意选了一个数字来开始游戏。
words.en: If you describe an action, rule, or decision as arbitrary, you think that it is not based on any principle, plan, or system. It often seems unfair because of this.

words.ex: The judge will arbitrate the dispute between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 法官将调解这两个邻居之间的纠纷。
words.en: To arbitrate means to officially settle a dispute by making a decision that both sides accept.

words.ex: They chose arbitration to solve their dispute.
words.ex_cn: 他们选择了仲裁来解决他们的纠纷。
words.en: Arbitration is a process in which a disagreement between two people or groups is settled by an arbitrator.

words.ex: The arbitrator helped the two sides reach an agreement.
words.ex_cn: 仲裁员帮助双方达成了协议。
words.en: An arbitrator is a person who has been officially chosen to make a decision between two people or groups who do not agree.

words.ex: The arboreal squirrel climbs high in the trees.
words.ex_cn: 这种树栖松鼠在高高的树上攀爬。
words.en: Relating to trees; living in trees.

words.tr:
v. 成弧线；
n. 弧；弧形物；
words.ex: The rainbow arcs across the sky.
words.ex_cn: 彩虹在天空中形成一道弧线。
words.en: An arc is a smoothly curving line or movement.

words.ex: The bridge has a stone arch.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥有一个石拱。
words.en: An arch is a structure that is curved at the top and is usually made of stone or brick. Arches are often used to support the weight of a bridge or the roof of a building.

words.ex: The archaeologist found an old pot in the ground.
words.ex_cn: 这位考古学家在地下发现了一个旧陶罐。
words.en: An archaeologist is someone who studies the societies and cultures of the past by examining the remains of their buildings, tools, and other objects.

words.ex: He loves archaeology and digs old artifacts.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱考古学，挖掘古代文物。
words.en: Archaeology is the study of the societies and peoples of the past by examining the remains of their buildings, tools, and other objects.

words.ex: The word 'thou' is archaic in modern English.
words.ex_cn: ‘thou’这个词在现代英语中是过时的。
words.en: Very old or old-fashioned.

words.ex: He is an architect who designs houses.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位设计房屋的建筑师。
words.en: An architect is a person who designs buildings and advises in their construction.

words.ex: He studies architecture at university.
words.ex_cn: 他在大学学习建筑学。
words.en: Architecture is the art and science of designing buildings and other physical structures.

words.ex: The old letters are kept in the city archives.
words.ex_cn: 这些旧信件保存在城市的档案馆里。
words.en: A collection of historical documents or records providing information about a place, institution, or group of people.

words.tr:
n. 北极地区；
adj. 北极的；
words.ex: Polar bears live in the arctic.
words.ex_cn: 北极熊生活在北极地区。
words.en: The Arctic is the area around the Earth's North Pole, characterized by cold temperatures and ice.

words.ex: He is an ardent supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心支持者。
words.en: An ardent person has strong feelings or enthusiasm for something.

words.ex: Climbing the mountain was an arduous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰巨的任务。
words.en: Something that is arduous is difficult and tiring, and involves a lot of effort.

words.ex: The area of the rectangle is 20 square meters.
words.ex_cn: 这个矩形的面积是20平方米。
words.en: An area is a particular part of a place, piece of land, or country.

words.ex: The boxing match took place in an arena.
words.ex_cn: 拳击比赛在竞技场举行。
words.en: An arena is a place or scene of activity, debate, or conflict, especially one where a competition or performance is held.

words.tr: v. 指出；表明；争论；争辩；
words.ex: He argued that the plan was too expensive.
words.ex_cn: 他指出这个计划太昂贵了。
words.en: If one person argues with another, they speak angrily to each other about something that they disagree about. You can also say that two people argue.

words.ex: His argument was clear and logical.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点清晰而有逻辑。
words.en: An argument is a discussion or debate in which people express different opinions about something.

words.ex: A problem arose during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 会议中出现了一个问题。
words.en: If a situation or problem arises, it begins to exist or people start to become aware of it.

words.tr: n. 贵族政治；贵族统治；贵族
words.ex: The aristocracy lived in big castles long ago.
words.ex_cn: 很久以前，贵族住在巨大的城堡里。
words.en: The highest class in certain societies, especially those holding hereditary titles or offices.

words.ex: The aristocrat lived in a big castle.
words.ex_cn: 这位贵族住在一座大城堡里。
words.en: An aristocrat is a person of high rank in a society, especially one who inherits a title and lands.

words.ex: He wears aristocratic clothes to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着贵族风格的衣服去参加派对。
words.en: Belonging to or characteristic of the aristocracy.

words.ex: He does arithmetic every day with his little sister.
words.ex_cn: 他每天和妹妹一起做算术。
words.en: Arithmetic is the part of mathematics that deals with the addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division of numbers.

words.tr:
n. 手臂；
v. 武装；
words.ex: He raised his arm to wave hello.
words.ex_cn: 他举起手臂打招呼。
words.en: An arm is one of the two long parts of your body that are attached to your shoulders and that have your hands at the end.

words.ex: He sits in the armchair and reads the newspaper.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在扶手椅上读报纸。
words.en: An armchair is a comfortable chair with sides that support your arms.

words.ex: The knight wore heavy armour in the battle.
words.ex_cn: 骑士在战斗中穿着沉重的盔甲。
words.en: Armour is a protective covering that is used to prevent damage from being inflicted to an object, individual, or vehicle by direct contact weapons or projectiles, usually during combat.

words.tr: n. 手臂；武器；兵器；“arm”的复数；
words.ex: He raised his arms to wave at the plane.
words.ex_cn: 他举起手臂向飞机挥手。
words.en: Weapons, especially as used by the military.

words.ex: The army trains new soldiers every month.
words.ex_cn: 军队每个月训练新兵。
words.en: An army is a large organized group of people who are armed and trained to fight on land in a war.

words.ex: The aroma of fresh bread filled the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 新鲜面包的香味充满了厨房。
words.en: An aroma is a strong, pleasant smell.

words.tr:
prep. 在…周围；环绕；
adv. 大约；到处；在附近；环绕；
words.ex: The children are running around the tree.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在树周围跑。
words.en: In a position or direction surrounding, or in the vicinity of, a particular place or thing.

words.ex: The movie aroused his curiosity.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影激起了他的好奇心。
words.en: If something arouses a particular reaction or attitude in people, it causes them to have that reaction or attitude.

words.ex: I will arrange a meeting for tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我将为明天安排一次会议。
words.en: If you arrange an event or meeting, you make plans for it to happen.

words.ex: We made an arrangement to meet at 6 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 我们安排好晚上六点见面。
words.en: An arrangement is a plan or preparation which you make so that something can happen.

words.ex: There was an array of people at the concert.
words.ex_cn: 音乐会上人山人海。
words.en: An array of different things or people is a large number or wide range of them.

words.ex: He paid off his arrear last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周还清了欠款。
words.en: Arrears are amounts of money that are owed and should have been paid earlier.

words.ex: The police arrested the thief last night.
words.ex_cn: 警察昨晚逮捕了那个小偷。
words.en: If the police arrest you, they take charge of you and take you to a police station, because they believe you may have committed a crime.

words.ex: The arrival of the train was delayed by 20 minutes.
words.ex_cn: 火车的到达晚了20分钟。
words.en: The act of coming to a place or the moment when something or someone arrives.

words.ex: He arrives at the station at 8 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 他早上8点到达车站。
words.en: To reach a place, especially at the end of a journey.

words.ex: His arrogance made others dislike him.
words.ex_cn: 他的傲慢让其他人不喜欢他。
words.en: Arrogance is the quality of being arrogant, which means having or revealing an exaggerated sense of one's own importance or abilities.

words.ex: He gave an arrogant answer to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他傲慢地回答了老师的问题。
words.en: Someone who is arrogant behaves in a proud, unpleasant way towards other people because they believe that they are more important than others.

words.ex: He behaved arrogantly towards his subordinates.
words.ex_cn: 他对下属表现得非常傲慢。
words.en: In a manner that shows an offensive attitude of superiority.

words.ex: The hunter shot an arrow at the target.
words.ex_cn: 猎人向目标射了一支箭。
words.en: An arrow is a long thin weapon which is sharp and pointed at one end and which often has feathers at the other end. Arrows are shot from a bow.

words.ex: He loves to paint and study art.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢绘画和学习艺术。
words.en: Art consists of paintings, sculpture, and other pictures or objects which are created for people to look at and admire or think deeply about.

words.ex: The artery carries blood from the heart.
words.ex_cn: 动脉将血液从心脏输送到身体。
words.en: An artery is a tube that carries blood from the heart to the rest of the body.

words.ex: He has arthritis in his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他双手有关节炎。
words.en: Arthritis is a medical condition in which the joints in someone's body are swollen and painful.

words.ex: He wrote an article about climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于气候变化的文章。
words.en: An article is a piece of writing on a particular subject in a newspaper, magazine, or online. It can also refer to a particular item or object, or a clause in a legal document.

words.ex: He can articulate his ideas clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的想法。
words.en: If you describe someone as articulate, you mean that they are able to express their thoughts and ideas easily and clearly.

words.ex: The flowers in the garden are artificial.
words.ex_cn: 花园里的花是人造的。
words.en: Made or produced by human beings rather than occurring naturally, especially as a copy of something natural.

words.ex: The army used artillery to attack the enemy base.
words.ex_cn: 军队用火炮攻击了敌方基地。
words.en: Artillery refers to large-caliber guns used in warfare on land.

words.ex: The artist painted a beautiful landscape.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家画了一幅美丽的风景画。
words.en: An artist is someone who draws or paints pictures or creates sculptures as a job or hobby.

words.ex: He is an artistic boy who loves to draw.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢画画的艺术型男孩。
words.en: Someone who is artistic is good at drawing or painting, or arranging things in a beautiful way.

words.tr:
adv. 如同；和…一样
prep. 作为；如同
conj. 由于；像；当…时；尽管
words.ex: He runs as fast as a cheetah.
words.ex_cn: 他跑得像猎豹一样快。
words.en: used to compare two things, to show that they are similar in some way; used to introduce the reason for something; used to mean 'in the role of'

words.tr: phrase. 迄今为止；到那时为止
words.ex: He has not finished his homework as yet.
words.ex_cn: 他还没有完成作业。
words.en: Up to the present time; until now.

words.ex: The balloon will ascend into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 气球将升上天空。
words.en: If you ascend a hill or staircase, you go up it. If a staircase or path ascends, it leads up to a higher place.

words.ex: The ascent of the mountain took all day.
words.ex_cn: 登这座山花了一整天。
words.en: An ascent is an act of climbing or moving upwards, or a path or slope that leads upwards.

words.ex: The detective tried to ascertain the truth.
words.ex_cn: 侦探试图查明真相。
words.en: If you ascertain the truth about something, you find out what it is, especially by making a deliberate effort to do so.

words.ex: They ascribe his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他们把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you ascribe an event or condition to a particular cause, you say or consider that it was caused by that thing.

words.tr: n. 东南亚国家联盟（Association of Southeast Asian Nations）
words.ex: ASEAN meets every year to discuss trade.
words.ex_cn: 东盟每年开会讨论贸易。
words.en: ASEAN, officially the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, is a political and economic union of 10 member states in Southeast Asia, which promotes intergovernmental cooperation and facilitates economic, political, security, military, educational, and sociocultural integration among its members and other countries in Asia.

words.ex: The fire left ash on the ground.
words.ex_cn: 火在地面上留下了灰烬。
words.en: the powdery residue left after the burning of a substance

words.ex: He felt ashamed for lying to his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他因为对妈妈撒谎而感到羞愧。
words.en: If someone is ashamed, they feel embarrassed or guilty because of something they have done or because of their appearance.

words.ex: The sailors swam ashore after the boat sank.
words.ex_cn: 船沉没后，水手们游到了岸上。
words.en: If someone or something comes ashore, they come from the sea onto the shore.

words.ex: He put the cigarette in the ashtray.
words.ex_cn: 他把香烟放进烟灰缸里。
words.en: An ashtray is a small dish in which smokers can put the ash from their cigarettes or cigars.

words.ex: He travels to Asia every summer.
words.ex_cn: 他每年夏天都去亚洲旅行。
words.en: Asia is the largest of the world's continents, covering approximately 30 percent of the Earth's land area. It is also the world's most populous continent, with roughly 60 percent of the total population.

words.tr:
adj. 亚洲的；
n. 亚洲人；
words.ex: He eats asian food every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天吃亚洲食物。
words.en: relating to Asia or its people, customs, or languages

words.ex: He stepped aside to let the bus pass.
words.ex_cn: 他走到一旁，让公交车通过。
words.en: If you move something aside, you move it to one side of you, usually because it is in the way.

words.ex: He asks me a question every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天问我一个问题。
words.en: If you ask someone something, you say something to them in the form of a question because you want to know the answer.

words.ex: The baby is asleep in the crib.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿在婴儿床里睡着了。
words.en: If someone is asleep, they are sleeping.

words.ex: One aspect of learning English is practicing speaking.
words.ex_cn: 学习英语的一个方面是练习口语。
words.en: An aspect of something is one of the parts of its character or nature.

words.ex: His aspiration is to become a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他的渴望是成为一名医生。
words.en: A strong desire to achieve something high or great.

words.tr: v. 向往；渴望；追求；立志
words.ex: He aspires to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他向往成为一名医生。
words.en: If you aspire to something, you have a strong desire to achieve it or attain it.

words.tr: n. 阿司匹林（镇痛解热消炎药）
words.ex: He took aspirin for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了阿司匹林来缓解头痛。
words.en: Aspirin is a common drug that is used to reduce pain and inflammation.

words.ex: The farmer rides his ass to the market.
words.ex_cn: 农夫骑着他的驴去市场。
words.en: An ass is a donkey, a domesticated animal of the horse family, or a foolish or stupid person.

words.ex: The king was assassinated by a secret group.
words.ex_cn: 国王被一个秘密组织刺杀。
words.en: To assassinate someone means to murder them, especially for political reasons or for payment.

words.ex: The king's assassination shocked the whole country.
words.ex_cn: 国王的暗杀震惊了整个国家。
words.en: The act of killing someone important or famous, often for political reasons.

words.ex: The assassinator was caught by the police.
words.ex_cn: 刺客被警察抓住了。
words.en: An assassinator is a person who murders an important person for political or religious reasons.

words.ex: The police investigated the assault on the old man.
words.ex_cn: 警方调查了对那位老人的攻击。
words.en: An assault is a physical attack on someone, or a military attack on a place.

words.ex: He will assemble the toy for his son.
words.ex_cn: 他将为儿子组装玩具。
words.en: If people assemble or if someone assembles them, they come together in a group, usually for a particular purpose such as a meeting.

words.ex: The assembly of the car took three days.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的装配花了三天时间。
words.en: An assembly is a group of people gathered together for a particular purpose, such as a meeting or a legislative session. It can also refer to the process of fitting together the component parts of a machine or other object.

words.tr: v. 断言；宣称；坚持；维护
words.ex: He asserts that the answer is correct.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持认为答案是正确的。
words.en: To state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully.

words.ex: His assertion was simple: the project will finish on time.
words.ex_cn: 他的断言很简单：项目会按时完成。
words.en: A statement that is made with confidence but without proof.

words.ex: The teacher will assess your homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会评估你的作业。
words.en: to judge or decide the amount, value, quality, or importance of something

words.ex: The teacher gave an assessment of the students' work.
words.ex_cn: 老师对学生的作品进行了评估。
words.en: An assessment is a judgment about something, especially about how good or bad it is, or an amount that is calculated for something, especially for tax purposes.

words.tr: n. 有价值的人或物；长处；
words.ex: He is an asset to the team because he works hard.
words.ex_cn: 他是个有价值的人，因为他工作努力。
words.en: An asset is something valuable that an individual, corporation, or country owns or controls with the expectation that it will provide a future benefit.

words.ex: The teacher will assign homework today.
words.ex_cn: 老师今天会布置作业。
words.en: To give someone a particular job or task; to allocate a resource or responsibility to a particular person or purpose.

words.ex: The teacher gave us a math assignment.
words.ex_cn: 老师给我们布置了一份数学作业。
words.en: An assignment is a task or piece of work that you are given to do, especially as part of your job or studies.

words.ex: He tries to assimilate new words every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天努力吸收新单词。
words.en: To assimilate means to take in and understand fully ideas, information, or culture, or to make something become part of a group or system.

words.ex: He assists his brother with homework.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助弟弟做作业。
words.en: If you assist someone, you help them to do a job or task by doing part of the work for them.

words.ex: He asked for assistance with his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他请求帮助做作业。
words.en: The act of helping or supporting someone or something.

words.ex: The teacher has an assistant to help with grading.
words.ex_cn: 老师有一个助理帮忙批改作业。
words.en: An assistant is a person who helps in particular work or who is under the authority of another person.

words.tr:
v. 把…联系在一起；
adj. 副的；
n. 同事；伙伴；
words.ex: He associates happiness with family time.
words.ex_cn: 他把幸福与家庭时光联系在一起。
words.en: If you associate someone or something with a particular quality or idea, or if they are associated with it, you connect them in your mind with that quality or idea.

words.tr: adj. 有关联的；相关的；联合的； v. 联想；联合；“associate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The two events are associated with each other.
words.ex_cn: 这两个事件是有关联的。
words.en: If one thing is associated with another, the two things are connected in some way.

words.ex: He joined a local book association.
words.ex_cn: 他加入了一个本地的图书协会。
words.en: An association is an official group of people who have the same job, aim, or interest.

words.ex: He has an associative memory that links colors to sounds.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种联想记忆，能把颜色和声音联系起来。
words.en: Relating to or resulting from association; involving the connection of ideas, feelings, or events.

words.tr: adj. 混杂的；什锦的；各样的
words.ex: He bought assorted candies at the store.
words.ex_cn: 他在商店买了各种各样的糖果。
words.en: Assorted means consisting of various kinds mixed together.

words.ex: The store offers an assortment of snacks.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店提供各种各样的零食。
words.en: An assortment is a group of similar things that are of different types or sizes.

words.ex: I assume it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我假定明天会下雨。
words.en: If you assume that something is true, you accept that it is true without proof.

words.ex: His assumption was that the train would be on time.
words.ex_cn: 他的假设是火车会准时。
words.en: An assumption is something that you assume to be the case, even without proof.

words.ex: He gave me his assurance that the work would be done on time.
words.ex_cn: 他向我保证工作会按时完成。
words.en: If you give someone an assurance that something is true or will happen, you say that it is definitely true or will definitely happen, in order to make them feel less worried.

words.ex: I assure you that everything will be fine.
words.ex_cn: 我向你保证一切都会好起来的。
words.en: If you assure someone that something is true or will happen, you tell them that it is definitely true or will definitely happen, often in order to make them less worried.

words.tr: adj. 确定的； v. 向…保证；“assure”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was assured that the package would arrive tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他确定包裹明天会到。
words.en: If you are assured of something, you are certain to get it or achieve it.

words.tr:
n. 星号
v. 给…注上星号
words.ex: She put an asterisk next to the word.
words.ex_cn: 她在那个词旁边加了一个星号。
words.en: An asterisk is a symbol (*) used in text to indicate a footnote or to highlight something important.

words.ex: He has asthma and cannot run fast.
words.ex_cn: 他有哮喘，不能跑快。
words.en: A respiratory condition marked by spasms in the bronchi of the lungs, causing difficulty in breathing. It usually results from an allergic reaction or other forms of hypersensitivity.

words.ex: The magic trick will astonish you.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术会让你惊讶。
words.en: If something or someone astonishes you, they surprise you very much.

words.ex: He stared in astonishment at the magic trick.
words.ex_cn: 他惊讶地盯着那个魔术。
words.en: Astonishment is a feeling of great surprise.

words.ex: The magic trick astounded the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让孩子们惊呆了。
words.en: If something astounds you, it surprises or shocks you very much.

words.tr:
adv. 迷路地；误入歧途地
adj. 迷路的；误入歧途的
words.ex: The little dog went astray in the park.
words.ex_cn: 那只小狗在公园里走丢了。
words.en: If you go astray, you lose your direction when you are trying to go somewhere.

words.ex: He reads his horoscope every morning because he believes in astrology.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都看星座运势，因为他相信占星术。
words.en: Astrology is the study of the movements and relative positions of celestial bodies interpreted as having an influence on human affairs and the natural world.

words.ex: The astronaut walked on the moon.
words.ex_cn: 这名宇航员在月球上行走。
words.en: An astronaut is a person who is trained to travel in a spacecraft.

words.ex: The astronomer looks at stars through a telescope.
words.ex_cn: 这位天文学家通过望远镜观察星星。
words.en: An astronomer is a scientist who studies celestial bodies such as planets, stars, and galaxies.

words.ex: He uses an astronomical telescope to watch stars.
words.ex_cn: 他用一架天文望远镜观察星星。
words.en: If you describe an amount, especially the cost of something as astronomical, you are emphasizing that it is very large indeed.

words.ex: He loves watching stars and learning astronomy.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢看星星并学习天文学。
words.en: Astronomy is the scientific study of celestial objects, space, and the physical universe as a whole.

words.tr: n. 收容所；避难所；精神病院；（政治）庇护
words.ex: The old building now serves as an asylum for the homeless.
words.ex_cn: 这栋旧建筑现在是无家可归者的收容所。
words.en: An asylum is a place where people who are in danger or who have no homes can go for safety and protection.

words.tr: adj. 不对称的；不均匀的
words.ex: The two sides of the box are asymmetric.
words.ex_cn: 盒子的两边不对称。
words.en: An asymmetric object does not have the same shape, size, or arrangement on both sides of a central line.

words.ex: The painting has asymmetry in its design.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画的构图不对称。
words.en: The quality of being asymmetrical; lack of symmetry.

words.ex: He threw the ball at the window.
words.ex_cn: 他把球朝窗户扔去。
words.en: You use at to indicate the place or event where something happens or is situated.

words.tr: n. 运动员；田径运动员；
words.ex: The athlete ran fast and won the race.
words.ex_cn: 这位运动员跑得很快，赢得了比赛。
words.en: An athlete is a person who is proficient in sports and other forms of physical exercise.

words.tr: adj. 运动的；身强力壮的；
words.ex: He is an athletic boy who loves running.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个热爱跑步的运动型男孩。
words.en: Athletic is used to describe someone who is physically strong, fit, and good at sports, or something related to sports or physical activities.

words.tr:
n. 大西洋；
adj. 大西洋的；
words.ex: The ship crossed the Atlantic in ten days.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船用了十天时间穿越大西洋。
words.en: The Atlantic is the ocean that lies between the Americas to the west and Europe and Africa to the east.

words.ex: He looked up the country in an atlas.
words.ex_cn: 他在地图册里查找那个国家。
words.en: An atlas is a book of maps or charts.

words.ex: The atmosphere keeps the Earth warm.
words.ex_cn: 大气使地球保持温暖。
words.en: The atmosphere is the layer of gases surrounding a planet or other material body, held in place by the gravity of the body.

words.ex: The atmospheric pressure dropped before the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴来临前，大气压下降了。
words.en: Relating to the atmosphere of the Earth or another planet; creating a distinctive mood, typically of romance or nostalgia.

words.ex: The atom is the smallest part of matter.
words.ex_cn: 原子是物质的最小单位。
words.en: An atom is the smallest unit of ordinary matter that forms a chemical element. Every solid, liquid, gas, and plasma is composed of neutral or ionized atoms.

words.ex: The atomic structure of hydrogen is simple.
words.ex_cn: 氢的原子结构很简单。
words.en: relating to atoms or the energy that comes from splitting atoms

words.ex: Please attach the file to the email.
words.ex_cn: 请将文件附加到邮件中。
words.en: To attach something to something else means to fasten or join it to the other thing.

words.tr: n. 依恋；附件；附加装置；
words.ex: The child showed strong attachment to his teddy bear.
words.ex_cn: 孩子对他的泰迪熊产生了强烈的依恋。
words.en: An attachment is a file that is sent along with an email message.

words.tr:
n. 攻击；袭击；
v. 攻击；袭击；
words.ex: The attack happened at night.
words.ex_cn: 这次攻击发生在夜晚。
words.en: To attack means to try to hurt or defeat someone or something by using force or violence.

words.ex: He worked hard to attain his goals.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以达到他的目标。
words.en: If you attain something, you gain it or achieve it, often after a lot of effort.

words.tr:
n. 企图；试图；
v. 企图；试图；
words.ex: His attempt to cheat on the test failed.
words.ex_cn: 他企图在考试中作弊，但失败了。
words.en: To make an effort to achieve or complete something, especially something difficult.

words.tr: v. 出席；参加；注意；照料；
words.ex: He will attend the meeting tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会出席会议。
words.en: To be present at an event, meeting, or function; to take care of or look after someone or something.

words.ex: His attendance at the meeting was mandatory.
words.ex_cn: 他必须出席这次会议。
words.en: The act of being present at a place or event.

words.tr:
n. 服务人员
adj. 随之而来的
words.ex: The attendant helped me find my seat.
words.ex_cn: 服务员帮我找到了座位。
words.en: An attendant is someone whose job is to serve or help people in a public place.

words.ex: The child needs attention when he does homework.
words.ex_cn: 孩子做作业时需要被关注。
words.en: Attention is the act of focusing your mind on something and taking notice of it.

words.tr: adj. 注意的；专心的；留心的；关心的
words.ex: The child is attentive in class.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子上课很专心。
words.en: If you are attentive, you are paying close attention to what is being said or done.

words.tr: adv. 注意地；聚精会神地；专心地
words.ex: She listened attentively to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 她专心地听老师讲课。
words.en: If you do something attentively, you do it with full concentration and focus.

words.ex: The children found old toys in the attic.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在阁楼上找到了旧玩具。
words.en: An attic is a space or room just below the roof of a building, often used for storage or as an extra room.

words.ex: His attitude toward homework is very positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对作业的态度非常积极。
words.en: An attitude is a way of thinking or feeling about something, which is often reflected in a person's behavior.

words.tr: n. 律师；辩护律师；代理人
words.ex: The attorney helped the man with his case.
words.ex_cn: 律师帮助那个人处理了他的案件。
words.en: An attorney is a lawyer who is qualified to represent a client in court.

words.ex: The bright flowers attract bees.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的花朵吸引蜜蜂。
words.en: If something or someone attracts you, they have particular qualities which cause you to like or admire them.

words.ex: The attraction of the city draws many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的吸引力吸引了许多游客。
words.en: An attraction is something that makes people want to go to a place or do a particular thing because they are interested in it.

words.ex: She is an attractive woman.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个有吸引力的女性。
words.en: An attractive person or thing is pleasing or appealing to look at.

words.ex: The accident is attributable to poor road conditions.
words.ex_cn: 这起事故可归因于糟糕的路况。
words.en: Capable of being attributed to someone or something.

words.tr:
v. 把…归因于；由…引起；
n. 品质；属性；特征；属性；
words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

words.ex: He gave attribution to the original writer.
words.ex_cn: 他把功劳归于原作者。
words.en: The action of regarding something as being caused by a person or thing.

words.ex: The word 'red' is an attributive in 'red car'.
words.ex_cn: 在 'red car' 中，'red' 是一个限定词。
words.en: An attributive adjective is an adjective that is placed before the noun it modifies, without a linking verb.

words.ex: The old painting was sold at an auction.
words.ex_cn: 那幅旧画在拍卖会上被卖出了。
words.en: An auction is a public sale where goods or property are sold to the highest bidder.

words.ex: The whisper was barely audible.
words.ex_cn: 那耳语几乎听不见。
words.en: If a sound is audible, it is loud enough for you to hear it.

words.ex: The audience clapped loudly after the show.
words.ex_cn: 演出结束后，观众热烈鼓掌。
words.en: The group of spectators at a public event; listeners or viewers collectively, especially those attending a performance or reading a particular work.

words.tr: adj. 视听的；视听教学的
words.ex: The school uses audio-visual tools to teach students.
words.ex_cn: 学校使用视听工具来教学。
words.en: Relating to both hearing and sight, or to equipment and materials used to provide such experiences, especially in education or entertainment.

words.ex: The company hired an expert to do an audit.
words.ex_cn: 公司聘请了一位专家进行审计。
words.en: An audit is an official examination of the accounts of a business or organization to check that they are accurate and correct.

words.tr:
n. 试听；试唱；试演；听力
v. 试听；试音；试镜；让…试演
words.ex: He went to an audition for the school play.
words.ex_cn: 他去参加学校话剧的试听。
words.en: An audition is a short performance given by an actor, dancer, or musician so that someone can decide if they are good enough to be in a play, film, or orchestra.

words.ex: The school concert was held in the auditorium.
words.ex_cn: 学校的音乐会是在礼堂举行的。
words.en: An auditorium is the part of a theatre, concert hall, or other public building in which the audience sits.

words.ex: She works out to augment her strength.
words.ex_cn: 她锻炼以增强力量。
words.en: If you augment something, you make it larger, stronger, or more effective by adding something to it.

words.ex: He was born in August.
words.ex_cn: 他出生在八月。
words.en: August is the eighth month of the Gregorian calendar, following July and preceding September.

words.ex: My aunt bought me a birthday gift.
words.ex_cn: 我姨给我买了一份生日礼物。
words.en: The sister of your father or mother, or the wife of your uncle.

words.ex: He passed the aural test by listening carefully.
words.ex_cn: 他通过仔细听通过了听力测试。
words.en: Relating to the ear or the sense of hearing.

words.ex: The clear sky was an auspice of good weather.
words.ex_cn: 晴朗的天空是好天气的预兆。
words.en: An auspice is a sign or omen that is believed to predict the future, often seen as favorable or supportive. It can also refer to the protection or support provided by a person or organization.

words.ex: She moved to Australia last year.
words.ex_cn: 她去年搬到了澳大利亚。
words.en: A country comprising the mainland of the Australian continent, the island of Tasmania, and numerous smaller islands.

words.ex: She bought an Australian sheepskin coat.
words.ex_cn: 她买了一件澳大利亚羊皮外套。
words.en: relating to Australia or its people

words.tr: adj. 真正的；真实的；真迹的；可靠的；
words.ex: This is an authentic painting by Picasso.
words.ex_cn: 这是一幅毕加索的真迹。
words.en: If something is authentic, it is real, true, or what people say it is.

words.ex: He is the author of this book.
words.ex_cn: 他是这本书的作者。
words.en: An author is a person who writes books, stories, or articles, especially as a job.

words.ex: The teacher gave an authoritative answer.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了一个权威性的回答。
words.en: If something is authoritative, it is respected and accepted as true or correct because it comes from a reliable source.

words.tr: n. 权威；官方机构；权力；权威人士；当局；
words.ex: The teacher is an authority on ancient history.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师是古代史方面的权威。
words.en: The power to make decisions or enforce rules.

words.ex: He needs authorization to enter the room.
words.ex_cn: 他需要获得授权才能进入房间。
words.en: Authorization is the act of giving someone the power or right to do something.

words.ex: The manager will authorize the payment tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 经理明天将批准这笔付款。
words.en: To give official permission for something to happen, or to give someone official permission to do something.

words.ex: He wrote his autobiography when he was 70.
words.ex_cn: 他70岁时写了自传。
words.en: An autobiography is a book about the life of a person, written by that person.

words.ex: The factory will automate the assembly line.
words.ex_cn: 工厂将自动化装配线。
words.en: To automate a factory, office, or industrial process means to put in machines which can do the work instead of people.

words.ex: The door opens automatically when you get close.
words.ex_cn: 当你靠近时，门会自动打开。
words.en: If something happens automatically, it happens as a part of the normal process or system, without needing to be started by someone.

words.ex: The factory uses automation to make cars.
words.ex_cn: 工厂使用自动化来制造汽车。
words.en: The use of largely automatic equipment in a system of manufacturing or other production process.

words.ex: He drives an automobile to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天开车去上班。
words.en: A vehicle that is powered by an engine and is used for carrying passengers on roads.

words.tr: adj. 自治的；有自治权的；自主的；
words.ex: The region has autonomous control over its education system.
words.ex_cn: 这个地区对其教育系统拥有自治权。
words.en: An autonomous organization, country, or region is independent and has the freedom to govern itself.

words.tr: n. 自主权；自治权；自治；
words.ex: The region demands autonomy from the central government.
words.ex_cn: 该地区要求从中央政府获得自主权。
words.en: Autonomy is the ability or condition of being self-governing; independence in one's thoughts or actions.

words.ex: Leaves fall in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 树叶在秋季落下。
words.en: Autumn is the season between summer and winter when leaves change color and the weather becomes cooler.

words.tr:
adj. 辅助的；附属的
n. 辅助物；附属物；助动词
words.ex: He used an auxiliary verb to form the past tense.
words.ex_cn: 他使用了一个助动词来构成过去时。
words.en: An auxiliary is a person or thing that provides additional help or support.

words.ex: He did not avail himself of the opportunity.
words.ex_cn: 他没有利用这个机会。
words.en: If you avail yourself of something, you use it or take advantage of it.

words.ex: The availability of free Wi-Fi is important for travelers.
words.ex_cn: 免费Wi-Fi的可用性对旅行者很重要。
words.en: The quality of being able to be used or obtained.

words.tr: adj. 可获得的；有空的；可用的；
words.ex: The books are available in the library.
words.ex_cn: 这些书在图书馆里可以借到。
words.en: If something is available, it is able to be used or obtained.

words.ex: Applications arrived in an avalanche after the job posting.
words.ex_cn: 职位发布后，申请纷至沓来。
words.en: An avalanche is a large mass of snow, ice, and rocks that falls quickly down the side of a mountain.

words.tr: v. 报（某事）之仇；为（某人）报仇
words.ex: He wants to avenge his brother's death.
words.ex_cn: 他想为弟弟的死报仇。
words.en: To avenge someone means to harm or punish someone who has harmed them or someone they care about.

words.ex: There are many shops on this avenue.
words.ex_cn: 这条大街上有许多商店。
words.en: An avenue is a wide street or main thoroughfare, often lined with trees or other landscaping.

words.tr:
n. 平均数；平均水平；
adj. 平均的；普通的；
v. 平均为…；
words.ex: The average of 4, 5, and 6 is 5.
words.ex_cn: 4、5和6的平均数是5。
words.en: An average is the result that you get when you add two or more numbers together and divide the total by the number of numbers you added together.

words.ex: He performs averagely in math tests.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学考试中表现一般。
words.en: In a manner that is typical or usual; to an average degree.

words.ex: He turned his head to avert the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他转过头去避免了事故。
words.en: If you avert something unpleasant, you prevent it from happening.

words.tr: n. 航空；航空学；飞行（术）；
words.ex: He works in aviation as a pilot.
words.ex_cn: 他作为一名飞行员从事航空工作。
words.en: Aviation is the operation and production of aircraft.

words.ex: He avoids eating sugar to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他避免吃糖以保持健康。
words.en: If you avoid something, you take action in order to prevent it from happening to you.

words.ex: I am awaiting the bus.
words.ex_cn: 我正在等公交车。
words.en: If you await someone or something, you wait for them.

words.ex: He stayed awake all night to finish his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他整晚醒着完成作业。
words.en: If you are awake, you are not sleeping. If you awake, you wake up.

words.tr: v. 唤醒；唤起；使意识到
words.ex: The loud noise awakened him.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音把他吵醒了。
words.en: If you awaken a feeling or emotion, or if it awakens, it starts to be felt or experienced.

words.tr:
n. 奖品；裁定；
v. 授予；
words.ex: He received an award for best student.
words.ex_cn: 他获得了最佳学生奖。
words.en: An award is a prize or other mark of recognition given in honor of an achievement.

words.ex: He is aware of the danger.
words.ex_cn: 他意识到危险。
words.en: If you are aware of something, you know about it.

words.ex: He walked away from the house.
words.ex_cn: 他远离了房子。
words.en: If someone or something moves or is moved away from a place, they move or are moved so that they are no longer there.

words.ex: The children stood in awe at the sight of the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到山时感到敬畏。
words.en: A feeling of reverential respect mixed with fear or wonder.

words.tr: adj. 棒极了；令人敬畏的；令人畏惧的；
words.ex: The concert was awesome!
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会棒极了！
words.en: If you describe someone or something as awesome, you are emphasizing that you think that they are very impressive or extraordinary.

words.tr:
adj. 糟糕的；可怕的；
adv. 非常；极其；
words.ex: The weather today is awful.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气很糟糕。
words.en: If you say that something is awful, you mean that it is extremely unpleasant, shocking, or bad.

words.tr: adv. 非常；很；令人畏惧地
words.ex: The weather is awfully cold today.
words.ex_cn: 今天天气冷得厉害。
words.en: Awfully is used to emphasize the degree or extent of something, often implying that it is more than expected or usual.

words.ex: He felt awkward when he forgot his friend's name.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记朋友的名字时，他感到很尴尬。
words.en: If you describe a situation as awkward, you mean that it is embarrassing or difficult to deal with.

words.tr: adv. 笨拙地；局促不安地；尴尬地
words.ex: He walked awkwardly after his injury.
words.ex_cn: 他受伤后走路很不自然。
words.en: In a manner that is not graceful or elegant in movement or shape; clumsily.

words.ex: Her awkwardness in social situations made her feel uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 她在社交场合的笨拙让她感到不自在。
words.en: The quality of being awkward; clumsiness or lack of grace.

words.ex: He picked up an axe to chop wood.
words.ex_cn: 他拿起一把斧子去砍柴。
words.en: An axe is a tool used for chopping wood, typically consisting of a heavy metal blade fixed at a right angle at the end of a long handle. As a verb, to axe means to dismiss or reduce something drastically.

words.ex: The axial wind blew strongly through the valley.
words.ex_cn: 轴向的风猛烈地吹过山谷。
words.en: Relating to or forming an axis; situated around, in the direction of, on, or along an axis.

words.ex: The Earth rotates around its axis.
words.ex_cn: 地球围绕其轴旋转。
words.en: An axis is an imaginary line through the middle of something, especially one that it turns around.

words.ex: The wheel fell off because the axle broke.
words.ex_cn: 车轮掉了，因为车轴断了。
words.en: An axle is a rod or spindle (either fixed or rotating) passing through the center of a wheel or group of wheels.

words.tr: abbr. 公元前；“before Christ”的缩写
words.ex: The pyramid was built in 2500 b.c.
words.ex_cn: 这座金字塔建于公元前2500年。
words.en: Before Christ; used to indicate that a date is before the Christian era.

words.ex: Bl is not a real word in English.
words.ex_cn: bl 不是英语中的真实单词。
words.en: A small, round mark or spot, often used as a punctuation mark or to indicate a position.

words.ex: The baby is sleeping in the crib.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿正在婴儿床里睡觉。
words.en: A baby is a very young child, especially one that cannot yet walk or talk.

words.tr: v. 临时照看；看管（婴孩）
words.ex: She baby-sits her neighbor's child every Friday.
words.ex_cn: 她每周五帮邻居照看孩子。
words.en: To care for a child or children while the parents are away, typically for a short period.

words.tr: n. 代人临时照看婴孩者
words.ex: She works as a baby-sitter on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 她在周末做保姆。
words.en: A person paid to look after a child or children while the parents are away.

words.ex: He earned a bachelor in computer science.
words.ex_cn: 他获得了计算机科学学士学位。
words.en: A bachelor is a man who has never been married.

words.tr:
adv. 回原处；向后；
n. 后面；背部；
v. 支持；
adj. 后面的；
words.ex: He put the book back on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 他把书放回了书架。
words.en: The back is the rear surface of the human body from the shoulders to the hips.

words.ex: He is the backbone of the team.
words.ex_cn: 他是团队的中坚。
words.en: The backbone is the most important part of something, providing support and strength.

words.tr: n. （推销员对顾客的）第二次访问
words.ex: The salesperson made a back-call to check if the customer was happy with the product.
words.ex_cn: 销售员进行了第二次访问，以确认顾客对产品是否满意。
words.en: A misspelling of 'callback', a return phone call or a follow-up contact in a professional context.

words.tr: v. 回溯；将日期追溯到过去某时
words.ex: They backdate the contract to last month.
words.ex_cn: 他们把合同的日期回溯到上个月。
words.en: To backdate a document or agreement means to make its effective date earlier than the current date.

words.ex: He changed his job because of his background.
words.ex_cn: 他因为自己的背景换了工作。
words.en: The background is the situation that exists at a particular time, or the situation in which something happens, which helps to explain it.

words.tr: n. 支持； v. 支持；“back”的现在分词；
words.ex: His backing helped the team win the match.
words.ex_cn: 他的支持帮助球队赢得了比赛。
words.en: Support or help.

words.tr: n. 积压未办之事；没交付的订货；存货
words.ex: The team has a big backlog of emails to answer.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队有一大堆待回复的邮件。
words.en: A backlog is a quantity of work that should have been done already, but has not yet been done.

words.tr:
adv. 向后地；
adj. 向后的；
words.ex: He walked backward to see the sign.
words.ex_cn: 他向后走以便看清楚那个标志。
words.en: If you move or look backward, you move or look in the direction that your back is facing.

words.tr: n. （无比较级）向后; 相反; 倒; 回顾
words.ex: The village still shows backwardness in using modern technology.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄在使用现代技术方面仍然落后。
words.en: The state of being behind in development or progress.

words.ex: He ate eggs and bacon for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐吃了鸡蛋和培根。
words.en: Bacon is a type of salt-cured pork made from various cuts, typically from the pork belly or from back cuts, which are less fatty than the belly.

words.ex: The bacterium causes sickness in humans.
words.ex_cn: 这种细菌会导致人类生病。
words.en: A bacterium is a very small organism which often causes disease.

words.tr: adj. 糟糕的；坏的；严重的；
words.ex: The weather today is bad.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气很糟糕。
words.en: If you describe something as bad, you mean that it is of a low or unacceptable standard or quality.

words.ex: He wears a badge on his shirt.
words.ex_cn: 他衬衫上戴着一枚徽章。
words.en: A badge is a small piece of metal, plastic, or cloth which you wear in order to show people that you have a particular rank, job, or belong to a particular group.

words.ex: He played badly in the game.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中表现得很差。
words.en: If something is done badly or goes badly, it is not successful or effective.

words.tr: n. 羽毛球运动；羽毛球；
words.ex: He plays badminton every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他每周末打羽毛球。
words.en: A game played with rackets and a shuttlecock, which is hit back and forth across a high net.

words.tr:
v. 使困惑；难倒；阻碍
n. 挡板；遮护物；阻碍体
words.ex: The magic trick baffled the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If something baffles you, you cannot understand it or explain it.

words.ex: She put the apples in a bag.
words.ex_cn: 她把苹果装进了一个袋子里。
words.en: A bag is a container made of flexible material with an opening at the top, used for carrying things.

words.ex: He carried his baggage to the airport.
words.ex_cn: 他把行李带到了机场。
words.en: Baggage refers to the suitcases and bags that you take with you when you travel, or it can refer to emotional issues that someone carries with them from past experiences.

words.tr: adj. 袋状的；宽松的；松弛垂落的
words.ex: He wears baggy jeans to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿宽松的牛仔裤去参加派对。
words.en: If a piece of clothing is baggy, it hangs loosely on your body.

words.tr:
n. 鱼饵；诱惑物
v. 下诱饵
words.ex: He used bread as bait to catch fish.
words.ex_cn: 他用面包当诱饵来钓鱼。
words.en: Bait is something which is used to attract fish or animals so that they can be caught. It can also refer to something that is offered to someone to persuade them to do something.

words.ex: She bakes bread every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 她每周日都烤面包。
words.en: To bake is to cook food using dry heat, especially in an oven.

words.ex: The baker makes bread every morning.
words.ex_cn: 面包师每天早上都做面包。
words.en: A baker is a person whose job is to bake bread, cakes, or pastries.

words.ex: I bought fresh bread from the bakery.
words.ex_cn: 我从面包房买了新鲜面包。
words.en: A bakery is a place where bread, cakes, and pastries are made or sold.

words.tr:
n. 平衡；天平；秤；
v. （使）相抵；（使）平衡；
words.ex: She maintains a good balance between work and rest.
words.ex_cn: 她在工作和休息之间保持良好的平衡。
words.en: Balance is the ability to remain steady when you are standing up. Also, it refers to the state of having your weight spread equally so that you do not fall. In finance, it refers to the amount of money you have in a bank account.

words.ex: He drinks coffee on the balcony every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都在阳台上喝咖啡。
words.en: A balcony is a platform on the outside of a building, enclosed by walls or balustrades, supported by columns or console brackets. The platform is projected from the wall of a building, usually above the ground floor.

words.tr: adj. 秃头的；不加修饰的；赤裸裸的
words.ex: The old man is bald.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人是秃头的。
words.en: Someone who is bald has little or no hair on the top of their head.

words.ex: The boy kicked the ball into the net.
words.ex_cn: 男孩把球踢进了网里。
words.en: A ball is a round object that is used in games such as soccer, baseball, and basketball. It can also refer to a formal dance.

words.ex: She practices ballet every afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 她每天下午练习芭蕾舞。
words.en: Ballet is a type of performance dance that originated during the Italian Renaissance in the 15th century and later developed into a concert dance form in France and Russia. It has since become a widespread, highly technical form of dance with its own vocabulary based on French terminology. It has been globally influential and has defined the foundational techniques used in many other dance genres.

words.tr: n. 气球；热气球；玩具气球；球状物；
words.ex: The child held a red balloon at the party.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在派对上拿着一个红色的气球。
words.en: A balloon is a small, thin, rubber bag that you blow air into so that it becomes larger and rounder or longer. Balloons are used as toys or decorations.

words.tr:
n. 气球驾驶；股票上涨；非法操作价格
v. 乘热气球飞行；膨胀；（使）激增；“balloon”的现在分词
words.ex: Ballooning is a popular hobby in the countryside.
words.ex_cn: 气球驾驶是乡村里一项受欢迎的爱好。
words.en: The act or sport of flying in a balloon. Also, the process of increasing rapidly in size or amount.

words.tr:
v. 进行无记名投票 
n. 无记名投票
words.ex: He cast his ballot in the election.
words.ex_cn: 他在选举中投了票。
words.en: A ballot is a process of voting, in writing and typically in secret. It is also the piece of paper on which you mark your vote.

words.ex: He writes with a ball-point pen.
words.ex_cn: 他用圆珠笔写字。
words.en: A pen with a small rotating ball at the tip that releases ink.

words.ex: They danced in the ballroom last night.
words.ex_cn: 昨晚他们在舞厅跳舞了。
words.en: A ballroom is a very large room that is used for dancing.

words.ex: He made a basket from bamboo.
words.ex_cn: 他用竹子做了一个篮子。
words.en: Bamboo is a tall tropical plant with hard, hollow stems. The young shoots of the plant can be eaten and the stems are used to make furniture.

words.ex: He eats bamboo-shoot for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐吃竹笋。
words.en: The young shoot of a bamboo plant, used as a vegetable in cooking.

words.tr:
v. 禁止；
n. 禁止；
words.ex: The school bans phones in class.
words.ex_cn: 学校禁止在课堂上使用手机。
words.en: If there is a ban on something, it is not allowed. If something is banned, it is not allowed to be done, shown, or used.

words.ex: He eats a banana every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃一根香蕉。
words.en: A banana is a long curved fruit with a yellow skin and soft, sweet, white flesh inside.

words.ex: The band is playing music.
words.ex_cn: 这个乐队在演奏音乐。
words.en: A band is a group of musicians who play music together, especially popular music. It can also refer to a strip of material used for binding or decoration, or a range of frequencies or wavelengths in a spectrum.

words.tr:
n. 绷带
v. 用绷带包扎
words.ex: He put a bandage on his cut finger.
words.ex_cn: 他在他割伤的手指上贴了绷带。
words.en: A bandage is a piece of material used to cover a wound or to support an injured part of the body.

words.ex: The bandit stole money from the bank.
words.ex_cn: 强盗从银行偷了钱。
words.en: A bandit is a person who robs people, especially one of a group of people who attack travelers.

words.ex: The bang woke me up at midnight.
words.ex_cn: 那声巨响在午夜把我吵醒了。
words.en: A bang is a sudden loud noise such as the noise of an explosion.

words.ex: The king banish the traitor from the kingdom.
words.ex_cn: 国王将叛徒驱逐出王国。
words.en: To banish someone means to send them away from a country or place and not allow them to return.

words.ex: I deposited money at the bank.
words.ex_cn: 我到银行存了钱。
words.en: A bank is an institution where people or businesses can keep their money or borrow money. It can also refer to the land alongside a river or lake.

words.tr: n. 银行家；经营银行业者；
words.ex: The banker gave him a loan to start a business.
words.ex_cn: 这位银行家给了他一笔贷款来创业。
words.en: A banker is a person who owns or manages a bank or has an important position in a bank.

words.tr: n. 银行业；银行业务； v. “bank”的现在分词；
words.ex: He works in banking in New York.
words.ex_cn: 他在纽约从事银行业。
words.en: Banking refers to the business activity of accepting and safeguarding money owned by other individuals and entities, and then lending out this money in order to earn a profit.

words.ex: The company is bankrupt after losing all its money.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司失去所有钱后破产了。
words.en: If a person or a company is bankrupt, they have been declared by a court of law to be unable to pay their debts.

words.tr: n. 破产；倒闭；无偿付能力
words.ex: The company filed for bankruptcy last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司去年申请了破产。
words.en: Bankruptcy is a legal status of a person or other entity that cannot repay the debts it owes to creditors.

words.ex: He waved a red banner in the parade.
words.ex_cn: 他在游行中挥舞着一面红旗子。
words.en: A banner is a long strip of cloth with a message or design on it, used especially for advertising or as a symbol of a particular group or cause.

words.ex: They had a big banquet after the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 婚礼后他们举办了一场盛大的宴会。
words.en: A banquet is a large formal meal for many people, often followed by speeches in honor of someone.

words.tr: n. 条状物；酒吧；栅栏；棒；
words.ex: He ate a chocolate bar after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后吃了一条巧克力。
words.en: A bar is a place where alcoholic drinks are served, or a long, narrow piece of metal or wood used for a particular purpose.

words.ex: We had a barbecue in the park last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 上周末我们在公园举行了户外烧烤。
words.en: A barbecue is a meal or gathering at which meat, fish, or other food is cooked out of doors on a rack over an open fire or on a special appliance.

words.ex: The barber cuts hair every day.
words.ex_cn: 理发师每天剪头发。
words.en: A barber is a person whose job is cutting men's hair and sometimes shaving their beards.

words.ex: The tree has bare branches in winter.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树在冬天有光秃秃的树枝。
words.en: If part of your body is bare, it is not covered by any clothing.

words.ex: He barely slept last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚几乎没睡觉。
words.en: You use barely to say that something is only just true or only just the case.

words.ex: I found a great bargain at the market.
words.ex_cn: 我在市场上找到了一件便宜货。
words.en: A bargain is an agreement between two people or groups in which each promises to do something in exchange for something else. It can also refer to something bought or offered for sale much more cheaply than is usual or expected.

words.ex: The barge carried coal down the river.
words.ex_cn: 驳船沿河运送煤炭。
words.en: A barge is a long, flat-bottomed boat used for carrying freight on canals and rivers.

words.tr:
n. 树皮；
v. 狗吠；
words.ex: The dog climbed the tree and touched the bark.
words.ex_cn: 狗爬上了树，摸了摸树皮。
words.en: The sound a dog makes; the outer covering of a tree.

words.ex: The farmer stores hay in the barn.
words.ex_cn: 农夫把干草存放在谷仓里。
words.en: A barn is a large building on a farm in which crops or animals are kept.

words.ex: The barometer shows that the weather will be fine.
words.ex_cn: 晴雨表显示天气会很好。
words.en: A barometer is an instrument that measures atmospheric pressure, used especially in forecasting the weather and determining altitude.

words.ex: The baron owns a large castle in the countryside.
words.ex_cn: 男爵拥有一座位于乡村的大城堡。
words.en: A baron is a man who is a member of the lowest rank of the nobility, or a powerful businessman with great influence in a particular industry.

words.tr: n. 男爵夫人；女男爵；（欧洲某些国家）男爵之女
words.ex: The baroness owns a large castle in the countryside.
words.ex_cn: 女男爵拥有一座位于乡村的大城堡。
words.en: A baroness is a woman who holds the rank of baron in her own right or is the wife or widow of a baron.

words.ex: He poured water into a wooden barrel.
words.ex_cn: 他把水倒进一个木桶里。
words.en: A barrel is a large, round container for liquids or food, typically made of wood or metal.

words.ex: The barren land cannot grow any crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片贫瘠的土地无法种植任何庄稼。
words.en: If you describe something as barren, you mean that it is not able to produce anything, especially plants or crops.

words.tr:
n. 路障；栅栏；阻碍
v. 设路障；阻挡
words.ex: The police put up a barricade to stop the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 警察设了一个路障来阻止人群。
words.en: A barricade is a temporary structure that is built across a road, entrance, or other route to prevent people from passing. It can also refer to the act of creating such a structure.

words.ex: The fence is a barrier to animals.
words.ex_cn: 这道围栏是动物的障碍。
words.en: A barrier is something such as a rule, law, or policy that makes it difficult or impossible for something to happen or be achieved.

words.tr: n. 物物交换；实物交易；
words.ex: They used barter to trade apples for eggs.
words.ex_cn: 他们用物物交换的方式用苹果换鸡蛋。
words.en: To trade goods or services without using money.

words.tr:
n. 基础；基地；
v. 以…为基础；
words.ex: The base of the building is very strong.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑的基础非常坚固。
words.en: The lowest part or edge of something, especially the part on which it rests or is supported.

words.ex: He plays baseball every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他每个周末打棒球。
words.en: a game played especially in North America by two teams of nine players, in which a player hits a ball with a bat and tries to run around four bases on a large field before the other team returns the ball

words.ex: The toys are in the basement.
words.ex_cn: 玩具在地下室里。
words.en: The basement of a building is a room or area that is partly or completely below ground level.

words.ex: This is a basic math skill.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个基本的数学技能。
words.en: You use basic to describe things, activities, and principles that are very important or necessary, and on which others depend.

words.ex: He basically just wants to be left alone.
words.ex_cn: 他基本上只是想一个人待着。
words.en: You use basically to indicate that you are stating a fact or opinion in a simple, clear, or definite way.

words.tr: n. 盆地；流域；水池；脸盆；
words.ex: The river flows into a large basin.
words.ex_cn: 河流流入一个巨大的盆地。
words.en: A basin is a large or small depression in the Earth's surface or a large container that holds water.

words.ex: The basis of math is numbers.
words.ex_cn: 数学的基础是数字。
words.en: The underlying support or foundation for an idea, argument, or process.

words.ex: She put the apples in a basket.
words.ex_cn: 她把苹果放进了一个篮子里。
words.en: A basket is a container which is usually made of stiff fibers, such as rushes, straw, or thin strips of wood, and is used for carrying or storing things.

words.ex: He plays basketball every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他每个周末打篮球。
words.en: A game played between two teams of five players in which goals are scored by throwing a ball through a netted hoop fixed above each end of the court.

words.ex: A bat flew out of the cave at night.
words.ex_cn: 一只蝙蝠在晚上从洞穴里飞了出来。
words.en: A bat is a piece of wood used to hit the ball in games such as cricket, baseball, and table tennis. It can also refer to a small animal that flies at night.

words.ex: The bakery made a new batch of bread this morning.
words.ex_cn: 这家面包店今天早上做了一批新面包。
words.en: A batch is a quantity or consignment of goods produced at one time.

words.ex: The bath is next to the bedroom.
words.ex_cn: 浴室在卧室旁边。
words.en: A bath is the process of washing your body, usually by sitting or lying in a container of water.

words.tr:
v. 沐浴；用水洗；沉浸
n. 游泳
words.ex: He bathes every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上洗澡。
words.en: To bathe means to wash oneself or someone else, especially in a bath or the sea, or to spend time in water for pleasure.

words.ex: I went to the bathroom after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 晚饭后我去了一趟浴室。
words.en: A room containing a bath or shower and typically also a washbasin and a toilet.

words.tr:
n. 击球员；
v. 连续猛击；
words.ex: The batter hit a home run in the ninth inning.
words.ex_cn: 击球员在第九局击出了全垒打。
words.en: To batter something means to hit it hard many times, often causing a lot of damage. In sports, a batter is the player who is trying to hit the ball in games like baseball or cricket. Batter can also refer to a mixture of flour, eggs, and milk or water, used to make pancakes or to coat food before frying.

words.ex: The remote needs a new battery.
words.ex_cn: 遥控器需要新电池。
words.en: A battery is a device that produces electricity to provide power for radios, cars, toys, etc.

words.tr:
n. 战斗；
v. 战斗；
words.ex: The soldiers fought in a long battle.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们进行了一场漫长的战斗。
words.en: A battle is a violent fight between groups of people, especially one between military forces during a war.

words.ex: The boat is parked in the bay.
words.ex_cn: 船停在海湾里。
words.en: A bay is a body of water partially enclosed by land, typically smaller than a gulf. It can also refer to a compartment for a ship, the color of a horse, or the sound a dog makes.

words.ex: We bought spices at the local bazaar.
words.ex_cn: 我们在当地的集市上买了香料。
words.en: A bazaar is a market consisting of rows of shops or stalls, especially in the Middle East, or a sale of miscellaneous contributed articles to benefit some charity.

words.ex: He is a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名老师。
words.en: Used to indicate the identity, qualities, or condition of someone or something.

words.ex: We walked on the beach at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 我们在日落时漫步在海滩上。
words.en: A beach is a landform along the coast of an ocean, sea, lake, or river. It usually consists of loose particles, which are often composed of rock, such as sand, gravel, shingle, pebbles, or cobblestones.

words.ex: She threaded a bead onto the string.
words.ex_cn: 她把一颗有孔的小珠穿在绳子上。
words.en: A bead is a small piece of glass, wood, or plastic that is used for decorating clothes or making jewellery.

words.ex: The bird uses its beak to eat seeds.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟用它的喙吃种子。
words.en: The hard, pointed, often curved part of a bird's mouth, used for picking up and eating food.

words.ex: The satellite beams signals to Earth.
words.ex_cn: 卫星向地球发射信号。
words.en: A beam is a long, thick piece of wood, metal, or concrete that is used to support the roof of a building. It can also refer to a line of light that shines from a bright object, or a smile that shows someone is very happy.

words.ex: He ate a bowl of beans for lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午餐吃了一碗豆子。
words.en: A bean is a seed from one of several genera of the flowering plant family Fabaceae, which are used for human or animal food.

words.tr:
n. 熊；
v. 承受；忍受；带有；生（孩子）；
words.ex: A bear walked near the campsite.
words.ex_cn: 一只熊在露营地附近走动。
words.en: If you bear something, you accept it and are able to deal with it, even though it is unpleasant or painful. A bear is a large, strong wild animal with thick fur and sharp claws.

words.ex: He grew a thick beard last winter.
words.ex_cn: 去年冬天他留了一脸浓密的胡须。
words.en: The hair that grows on a man's chin and cheeks.

words.tr: n. 影响；方位；轴承；举止； v. 忍受；“bear”的现在分词；
words.ex: The new policy has a big bearing on our daily lives.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策对我们日常生活有很大影响。
words.en: The manner in which one conducts or carries oneself, including posture and gestures; also refers to a machine part that supports another part and reduces friction.

words.tr: adj. 熊市的；（行情）看跌的
words.ex: He is bearish about the stock market.
words.ex_cn: 他对股市持看跌态度。
words.en: If someone is bearish about something, they think that it will fail or that it will be unsuccessful. In the stock market, if the market is bearish, prices are expected to fall.

words.ex: The beast ran fast through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 那只野兽在森林里快速奔跑。
words.en: A beast is a large and dangerous animal.

words.tr:
v. 打；敲打；击败；
n. 一击；跳动；
words.ex: He beat the drum loudly.
words.ex_cn: 他用力敲打鼓。
words.en: To defeat someone in a game, competition, election, or battle; to hit someone or something many times with your hand, a stick, etc.

words.ex: She works as a beautician at a local salon.
words.ex_cn: 她在一家本地美容院当美容师。
words.en: A beautician is a person whose job is to give people beauty treatments, for example, on their hair, skin, or nails.

words.ex: She is a beautiful girl.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个美丽的女孩。
words.en: Pleasing the senses or mind aesthetically.

words.tr: n. 美；美的事物；美丽；美人；
words.ex: The beauty of the sunset amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 日落的美让所有人都惊叹。
words.en: Beauty is the quality of being pleasing, especially to look at, or someone or something that gives great pleasure, especially when you look at it.

words.ex: He was late because the bus was slow.
words.ex_cn: 他迟到了，因为公交车很慢。
words.en: You use 'because' when stating the reason for something.

words.ex: The caterpillar becomes a butterfly.
words.ex_cn: 毛毛虫变成蝴蝶。
words.en: To begin to be something or to develop into something.

words.ex: He sleeps on a soft bed.
words.ex_cn: 他睡在一张柔软的床上。
words.en: A bed is a piece of furniture that you lie on when you sleep.

words.ex: He sleeps in his bedroom every night.
words.ex_cn: 他每晚都在卧室睡觉。
words.en: A bedroom is a room in a house or apartment where people sleep.

words.ex: The bee is flying near the flowers.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂正在花附近飞舞。
words.en: A bee is a flying insect known for its role in pollination and for producing honey and beeswax.

words.ex: He eats beef for dinner every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日吃牛肉当晚餐。
words.en: Beef is the meat from a cow, bull, or ox. When people beef about something, they complain about it.

words.ex: He drinks beer after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后喝啤酒。
words.en: Beer is an alcoholic drink made from grain.

words.ex: The beetle crawls on the leaf.
words.ex_cn: 甲虫在叶子上爬行。
words.en: A beetle is an insect with a hard shell-like back. Beetles are a group of insects which have a large number of species.

words.tr:
prep. 在…之前；先于；
conj. 在…以前；
adv. 以前；之前；
words.ex: She ate breakfast before school.
words.ex_cn: 她在上学之前吃了早餐。
words.en: Earlier in time; previously.

words.ex: Please tell me beforehand if you can't come.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不能来，请提前告诉我。
words.en: If you do something beforehand, you do it earlier than a particular event.

words.ex: He begs for food on the street.
words.ex_cn: 他在街上乞讨食物。
words.en: If you beg someone to do something, you ask them very anxiously or eagerly to do it.

words.ex: The beggar sat on the street with a cup.
words.ex_cn: 那个乞丐坐在街上，手里拿着一个杯子。
words.en: A beggar is a person who lives by asking people for money or food.

words.ex: He begins his homework after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后开始做作业。
words.en: To start doing something; to take the first step into a process or activity.

words.ex: He is a beginner in piano lessons.
words.ex_cn: 他是钢琴课的初学者。
words.en: A beginner is someone who has just started learning to do something and has not yet mastered it.

words.tr: n. 开头；开端； v. 开始；着手；“begin”的现在分词；
words.ex: The beginning of the story is very exciting.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的开头非常精彩。
words.en: The point in time or space at which something starts.

words.ex: He spoke on behalf of his team.
words.ex_cn: 他代表他的团队发言。
words.en: If you do something on someone's behalf, you do it for that person as their representative.

words.ex: The child behaves well in class.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子在课堂上表现得很好。
words.en: To behave means to act in a particular way, especially in a way that is good or correct.

words.ex: His behavior at the party was very polite.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上的举止非常礼貌。
words.en: The way in which one acts or conducts oneself, especially towards others.

words.tr:
prep. 在…后面；
adv. 在后面；
words.ex: The cat is behind the sofa.
words.ex_cn: 猫在沙发后面。
words.en: If something is behind a thing or person, it is on the far side of them as they face you, or is in a back part of them.

words.tr: adj. 拖欠的；落伍的，落后的；迟的; adv. 迟，慢；滞延
words.ex: He is behindhand with his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他的作业落下了。
words.en: If you are behindhand with something, you are late in doing it or you have not done as much of it as you should have by a particular time.

words.tr: v. “be”的现在分词；是；在； n. 存在；生物；人；生命；
words.ex: He is being quiet in the library.
words.ex_cn: 他正在图书馆里保持安静。
words.en: The state or quality of having existence.

words.ex: His belief in honesty never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他对诚实的信念从未改变。
words.en: A belief is a strong feeling that something is true or exists.

words.ex: I believe you are telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 我相信你在说真话。
words.en: If you believe in something, you think that it is true, or that it exists.

words.ex: The bell rang at 8 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 铃在早上八点响了。
words.en: A bell is a device that makes a ringing sound and is used to give a signal or to attract attention.

words.ex: He rubbed his belly after eating too much.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完太多后揉了揉腹部。
words.en: The belly is the front part of a person's or animal's body between the chest and the legs.

words.ex: This book belongs to me.
words.ex_cn: 这本书属于我。
words.en: If something belongs to you, you own it or it is yours.

words.ex: Her beloved dog always greeted her at the door.
words.ex_cn: 她钟爱的狗总是在门口迎接她。
words.en: Dearly loved.

words.tr:
prep. 在…下面；低于；少于；
adv. 在下面；
words.ex: The cat is below the table.
words.ex_cn: 猫在桌子下面。
words.en: If something is below something else, it is in a lower position.

words.ex: The factory uses a belt to move boxes.
words.ex_cn: 工厂使用传送带来运送箱子。
words.en: A belt is a strip of leather or other material worn around the waist to support clothes or for decoration.

words.ex: He sat on the bench in the park.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在公园的长凳上。
words.en: A bench is a long seat for several people, typically made of wood or metal.

words.tr:
n. 弯曲处；
v. （使）弯曲；
words.ex: The car turned at the bend in the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在道路的拐弯处转弯了。
words.en: To bend something means to change its shape so that it is no longer straight but curved.

words.ex: The cat is beneath the table.
words.ex_cn: 猫在桌子下面。
words.en: In or to a lower position than someone or something, under someone or something.

words.ex: Eating vegetables is beneficial to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吃蔬菜对你的健康有益。
words.en: Promoting or enhancing well-being; advantageous.

words.ex: He is the beneficiary of his father's will.
words.ex_cn: 他是他父亲遗嘱的受益人。
words.en: A beneficiary is someone who receives money or other benefits as a result of something, especially a will or insurance policy.

words.tr:
v. 有益于；有助于；
n. 利益；好处；
words.ex: Exercise benefits your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼有益于你的健康。
words.en: A benefit is something that helps you or improves your life in some way.

words.ex: His benevolence helped the poor family.
words.ex_cn: 他的仁慈帮助了这个贫困家庭。
words.en: The quality of being well meaning; kindness.

words.ex: The benevolent man gave food to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这位慈善的人给穷人提供了食物。
words.en: If you describe a person in authority as benevolent, you mean that they are kind and fair.

words.tr: adj. 弯曲的； v. 弯曲；使弯曲；“bend”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The bent pipe leaked water.
words.ex_cn: 弯曲的管道漏水了。
words.en: Bent is used to describe something that is not straight but has a curve or angle in it. It can also refer to someone's natural talent or inclination towards a particular activity or subject.

words.ex: Benzene is a chemical found in gasoline.
words.ex_cn: 苯是一种存在于汽油中的化学物质。
words.en: A colorless volatile liquid hydrocarbon present in coal tar and petroleum, used as a solvent and in the manufacture of numerous organic compounds.

words.ex: He picked a red berry from the bush.
words.ex_cn: 他从灌木丛中摘了一颗红色浆果。
words.en: A berry is a small, round fruit that grows on a bush or a tree. Some berries are edible and can be eaten raw or used in cooking.

words.tr:
n. 泊位；（船上的）卧铺
v. 停泊；占铺位
words.ex: The ship found a berth at the dock.
words.ex_cn: 船在码头找到了停泊位。
words.en: A berth is a bed on a boat, train, or other vehicle, or a place where a boat or ship can be tied up in a harbor.

words.ex: He was beset by problems at work.
words.ex_cn: 他被工作中的问题困扰。
words.en: If someone or something is beset by problems or fears, they have many problems or fears which affect them severely.

words.ex: He sat beside his friend on the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在朋友旁边。
words.en: At the side of; next to.

words.tr:
prep. 除…以外；
adv. 此外；
words.ex: Besides apples, he likes oranges.
words.ex_cn: 除了苹果，他还喜欢橙子。
words.en: In addition to; apart from.

words.ex: The bespectacled man read a book quietly.
words.ex_cn: 那位戴眼镜的男人安静地看书。
words.en: Wearing glasses; characterized by the wearing of glasses.

words.tr:
adj. 最好的；
adv. 最好地；
n. 最佳物；佼佼者；最高水平；
words.ex: He is the best player on the team.
words.ex_cn: 他是队里最好的球员。
words.en: Of the most excellent, effective, or desirable type or quality.

words.ex: The king will bestow a medal on the hero.
words.ex_cn: 国王将把奖章授予这位英雄。
words.en: To bestow something on someone means to give or present it to them.

words.ex: This book is a best-seller in many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这本书在许多国家都是畅销书。
words.en: A best-seller is a book or other product that sells in very large numbers.

words.ex: This book is the best-selling novel this year.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是今年最畅销的小说。
words.en: A best-selling product or book is one that many people buy.

words.tr:
v. 敢说；
n. 打赌；赌注；
words.ex: I bet you didn't know that.
words.ex_cn: 我敢说你不知道那件事。
words.en: If you bet on the result of a horse race, football game, or other event, you give someone a sum of money which they give you back with extra money if the result is what you predicted, or which they keep if it is not.

words.tr: v. 背叛；出卖；泄露；暴露
words.ex: He betrays his friend by telling the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他通过泄露秘密背叛了朋友。
words.en: If you betray someone who loves or trusts you, your actions hurt and disappoint them.

words.ex: He felt deep pain from his friend's betrayal.
words.ex_cn: 他因朋友的背叛感到深深的痛苦。
words.en: The action of betraying one's country, a group, or a person; treachery.

words.tr: adj. 更好的；更优秀的；“good”的比较级； adv. 更好地；“well”的比较级； v. 胜过；使更佳；
words.ex: This shirt is better than the other one.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫比那件更好。
words.en: If something is better, it is of a higher standard, quality, or level than something else, or than it was before.

words.tr: adj. 较富裕的；境况较好的
words.ex: The better-off families can afford private schools.
words.ex_cn: 条件较好的家庭能负担得起私立学校。
words.en: In a more favorable position, especially in financial terms.

words.ex: The cat is sitting between the two chairs.
words.ex_cn: 猫坐在两把椅子之间。
