words.en: A memento is an object which you keep because it reminds you of a person or a special event.

words.ex: He wrote a memo to remind the team.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一封备忘录提醒团队。
words.en: A memo is a short official note that is sent by one person to another within the same company or organization.

words.ex: He wrote a memoir about his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一本关于自己童年的回忆录。
words.en: A memoir is a book or article that you write about someone who you have known, describing what you remember of them and of particular events in which you both took part.

words.ex: He wrote a memorandum about the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一份关于会议的备忘录。
words.en: A memorandum is a written proposal or reminder, especially in a business context.

words.ex: They placed a memorial at the site of the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他们在事故地点放置了一座纪念物。
words.en: A memorial is a structure or event established to remind people of a person or event.

words.ex: He tries to memorize the words every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天试着记住这些单词。
words.en: To memorize something means to learn it so well that you can remember it perfectly.

words.ex: His memory is very good; he remembers everything.
words.ex_cn: 他的记忆力很好；他什么都记得。
words.en: Memory is the faculty by which the mind stores and remembers information.

words.ex: The broken bridge is a menace to drivers.
words.ex_cn: 这座破桥对司机来说是个危险物。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is a menace, you mean that they are likely to cause serious harm.

words.ex: He will mend his broken shoe.
words.ex_cn: 他将修补他破掉的鞋子。
words.en: If you mend something that is broken or damaged, you repair it, so that it works properly or so that it looks like new again.

words.ex: He has a mental illness.
words.ex_cn: 他有心理疾病。
words.en: Relating to the mind or involving the process of thinking.

words.ex: His mentality changed after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他的心理状态发生了变化。
words.en: Your mentality is your attitudes and your way of thinking.

words.tr:
v. 提到；说到；
n. 提及；说起；
words.ex: He didn't mention the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他没有提到那场事故。
words.en: If you mention something, you say something about it, usually briefly.

words.ex: He looked at the menu and chose pasta.
words.ex_cn: 他看了菜单，选择了意大利面。
words.en: A menu is a list of the food that is available at a restaurant or café.

words.ex: He runs a mercantile shop in the old town.
words.ex_cn: 他在老城区经营一家商业店铺。
words.en: relating to trade or commerce; commercial.

words.tr:
adj. 唯利是图的；雇佣的
n. 雇佣兵；唯利是图者
words.ex: He works as a mercenary for money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了钱当雇佣兵。
words.en: A mercenary is a professional soldier hired to serve in a foreign army.

words.ex: The store sells cheap merchandise.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店出售廉价商品。
words.en: Goods to be bought and sold.

words.ex: The merchant sells fresh fruit every morning.
words.ex_cn: 商人每天早上卖新鲜水果。
words.en: A merchant is a person who buys and sells goods, especially one who owns a shop.

words.tr: adj. 仁慈的；慈悲的；宽大的
words.ex: The judge was merciful and gave him a small fine.
words.ex_cn: 法官很仁慈，只判了他一笔小额罚款。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as merciful, you mean that they show or have mercy.

words.tr:
adj. 多汞的；含汞的；易变的；灵活的；反复无常的
n. 汞制剂；水银剂
words.ex: His mercurial mood changes from happy to angry quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他多汞的情绪很快从高兴变到生气。
words.en: If you describe someone as mercurial, you mean that they frequently change their mind or mood without warning.

words.ex: The thermometer contains mercury.
words.ex_cn: 温度计里含有水银。
words.en: Mercury is a heavy, silvery-white metal that is liquid at room temperature. It is used in thermometers, barometers, and other scientific apparatus.

words.ex: The judge showed mercy and let him go free.
words.ex_cn: 法官仁慈地让他自由了。
words.en: If someone in authority shows mercy, they choose not to harm someone they have power over, or they forgive someone they have the right to punish.

words.ex: It was a mere mistake, not intentional.
words.ex_cn: 那只是一个小小的错误，并非故意的。
words.en: You use mere to emphasize how unimportant or inadequate something is, in comparison to the general situation you are describing.

words.ex: He is merely a student.
words.ex_cn: 他仅仅是个学生。
words.en: You use merely to emphasize that something is only what you say and not better, more important, or more exciting.

words.ex: The two companies will merge next year.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司明年将合并。
words.en: To combine or unite to form a single entity.

words.ex: The dessert consisted of a layer of meringue topped with fresh berries.
words.ex_cn: 这道甜点由一层蛋白酥饼和新鲜浆果组成。
words.en: A light, fluffy dessert made from beaten egg whites and sugar, often used as a topping for pies or baked into crisp shells.

words.ex: The merit of this plan is its simplicity.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划的优点是简单。
words.en: If something has merit, it has good or worthwhile qualities.

words.ex: The little girl drew a mermaid in the sea.
words.ex_cn: 小女孩画了一条海里的美人鱼。
words.en: A mermaid is a mythical sea creature with the head and upper body of a woman and the tail of a fish.

words.ex: The children are merry on Christmas day.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在圣诞节那天很开心。
words.en: If you describe someone's character or behavior as merry, you mean that they are happy and cheerful.

words.ex: The net is made of a fine mesh.
words.ex_cn: 这个网是由细密的网状物制成的。
words.en: A mesh is a material made of a network of wire or thread to catch or hold things, or to allow things to pass through it.

words.tr:
n. 脏乱；杂乱；
v. 弄糟；
words.ex: The room was a mess after the party.
words.ex_cn: 派对后房间一片狼藉。
words.en: A mess is a situation that is confused and full of problems, or something that is dirty or untidy.

words.ex: I got your message this morning.
words.ex_cn: 我今天早上收到了你的消息。
words.en: A message is a piece of information or a request that you send to someone or leave for them when you cannot speak to them directly.

words.ex: He sent a message through a messenger.
words.ex_cn: 他通过信使发送了一条消息。
words.en: A messenger is someone who carries messages from one person to another.

words.ex: His room is messy with clothes everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 他的房间很杂乱，衣服到处都是。
words.en: If you describe something as messy, you mean that it is untidy or dirty.

words.ex: His metabolism is very fast.
words.ex_cn: 他的新陈代谢非常快。
words.en: Metabolism is the set of life-sustaining chemical transformations within the cells of living organisms.

words.ex: He found a piece of metal in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他在花园里发现了一块金属。
words.en: Metal is a hard, shiny substance such as iron, gold, or steel.

words.ex: The metallic spoon felt cold in her hand.
words.ex_cn: 金属勺子在她手中感觉很冷。
words.en: Metallic means relating to or resembling metal or metals.

words.ex: He works in metallurgy at a steel factory.
words.ex_cn: 他在钢铁厂从事冶金工作。
words.en: Metallurgy is the scientific study of the extraction, refining, alloying, and fabrication of metals and of their structure and properties.

words.ex: Calling time a thief is a metaphor.
words.ex_cn: 把时间称为小偷是一种隐喻。
words.en: A metaphor is a figure of speech in which a word or phrase is applied to an object or action to which it is not literally applicable.

words.tr: adj. 流星的；大气的；昙花一现的；辉煌而短暂的
words.ex: The meteoric rise of the new star surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这位新星的流星般崛起让所有人感到惊讶。
words.en: If you use meteoric to describe something such as a rise to fame, you mean it happens very quickly and is very noticeable.

words.ex: The meteorologist predicts rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 气象学家预测明天会下雨。
words.en: A meteorologist is a scientist who studies the atmosphere and its phenomena, especially in relation to weather and weather forecasting.

words.ex: He works in meteorology and predicts the weather.
words.ex_cn: 他从事气象学工作，预测天气。
words.en: Meteorology is the scientific study of the atmosphere and of atmospheric conditions, especially as they relate to weather and weather forecasting.

words.tr: n. 米；公尺；仪表；计量仪；
words.ex: The table is two meters long.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子两米长。
words.en: A meter is a unit of length in the metric system, equal to 100 centimeters. It can also refer to a device that measures and records the quantity, degree, or rate of something, such as electricity or gas.

words.ex: He found a new method to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他找到了一种解决这个问题的新方法。
words.en: A method is a particular way of doing something.

words.ex: He is methodical in organizing his work.
words.ex_cn: 他在安排工作时很有条理。
words.en: If you describe someone as methodical, you mean that they do things carefully, thoroughly, and in order.

words.ex: The study uses a new methodology to collect data.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究使用了一种新的方法论来收集数据。
words.en: A methodology is a system of methods and principles for doing something, for example for teaching or for carrying out research.

words.tr: adj. 一丝不苟的；缜密的
words.ex: He is meticulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他仔细检查作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as meticulous, you mean that they do things very carefully and with great attention to detail.

words.ex: She meticulously cleaned every corner of the room.
words.ex_cn: 她异常细致地打扫了房间的每一个角落。
words.en: If you do something meticulously, you do it very carefully and with great attention to detail.

words.ex: The table is two metres long.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子两米长。
words.en: A metre is a unit of length in the metric system, equal to 100 centimetres.

words.ex: The country uses metric units for weight and distance.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家使用米制单位来衡量重量和距离。
words.en: A metric is a system of measurement that uses meters, liters, and grams as its basic units.

words.ex: He takes the metro to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天乘地铁去上班。
words.en: A metro is an underground railway system in a city.

words.tr: adj. 大都市的；大城市的；
words.ex: He lives in a metropolitan city like New York.
words.ex_cn: 他住在纽约这样的大都市。
words.en: Relating to or denoting a metropolis or large city, especially as the main city of a country or region.

words.ex: She ate delicious Mexican food at the restaurant.
words.ex_cn: 她在餐厅吃了美味的墨西哥食物。
words.en: Relating to Mexico or its people.

words.tr: n. 墨西哥（拉丁美洲国家）
words.ex: He lives in Mexico.
words.ex_cn: 他住在墨西哥。
words.en: Mexico is a country in the southern part of North America.

words.ex: The microbe causes sickness.
words.ex_cn: 这种微生物会引起疾病。
words.en: A microbe is a very small living thing, which you can only see if you use a microscope. Some microbes can cause diseases.

words.tr: n. 微观世界；小宇宙；缩影
words.ex: The classroom is a microcosm of society.
words.ex_cn: 教室是社会的一个缩影。
words.en: A microcosm is a small, representative system having analogies to a larger system in constitution, configuration, or development.

words.ex: He is learning microeconomics this semester.
words.ex_cn: 他这学期正在学习微观经济学。
words.en: Microeconomics is the part of economics concerned with single factors and the effects of individual decisions.

words.ex: He used microfilm to save old newspapers.
words.ex_cn: 他使用微缩胶片保存旧报纸。
words.en: Microfilm is a film on which documents or printed materials are photographed at a greatly reduced size for ease of storage.

words.ex: He spoke into the microphone to be heard clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他对着麦克风说话，以便被清楚地听到。
words.en: A microphone is a device that is used to make sounds louder or to record them.

words.tr: n. 微处理器；微处理机
words.ex: The computer has a fast microprocessor.
words.ex_cn: 这台电脑有一个快速的微处理器。
words.en: A microprocessor is a small chip that can process data and carry out instructions in a computer or other electronic device.

words.ex: He looks at the bug through a microscope.
words.ex_cn: 他通过显微镜观察这只虫子。
words.en: An instrument used for viewing objects that are too small to be seen by the naked eye, especially one that uses a combination of lenses to produce a magnified image.

words.ex: She heated the food in the microwave.
words.ex_cn: 她把食物放在微波炉里加热。
words.en: A microwave is a type of oven that cooks or heats food very quickly by using electromagnetic waves rather than heat.

words.ex: We eat lunch at midday.
words.ex_cn: 我们在中午吃午饭。
words.en: Midday is the middle part of the day, from noon until early afternoon.

words.tr:
n. 中间；
adj. 中间的；
words.ex: The ball stopped in the middle of the field.
words.ex_cn: 球停在了场地的中间。
words.en: The middle of something is the part of it that is equally distant from its edges or outer limits.

words.ex: The middleman helped the buyer and seller agree on a price.
words.ex_cn: 中间人帮助买家和卖家达成了价格协议。
words.en: A middleman is a person who arranges business or political deals between other people.

words.tr: adj. 中等的，普通的 adv. 中等地，普通地
words.ex: He is a middling player on the team.
words.ex_cn: 他是队里一个中等水平的球员。
words.en: Of average quality; neither very good nor very bad.

words.ex: The clock struck midnight.
words.ex_cn: 钟敲响了午夜。
words.en: Midnight is twelve o'clock in the middle of the night.

words.ex: He stood in the midst of the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他站在人群中间。
words.en: The middle part or point of something.

words.ex: His mien showed calm and confidence.
words.ex_cn: 他的神情显得平静而自信。
words.en: A person's mien is their general appearance and manner, which might give you an idea of their character or mood.

words.tr: v. 可能；也许；“may”的过去式； n. 强大力量；
words.ex: He might come to the party tonight.
words.ex_cn: 他今晚可能会来参加派对。
words.en: Might is used to indicate that something is possible or might happen, or to ask for permission in a polite way.

words.tr:
adj. 巨大的；强大的；
adv. 非常；
words.ex: The mighty river flows through the valley.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的河流流经山谷。
words.en: Possessing great power, strength, or force; formidable.

words.ex: The migrant found a new job in the city.
words.ex_cn: 这位移居者在城市里找到了一份新工作。
words.en: A migrant is a person who moves from one place to another, especially in order to find work.

words.ex: Birds migrate south in winter.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类在冬天迁徙到南方。
words.en: If people migrate, they move from one place to another, especially in order to find work or to live somewhere for a short time.

words.ex: Birds begin migration in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类在秋天开始迁徙。
words.en: The movement of people, animals, or birds from one place to another, especially regularly according to the seasons.

words.ex: Birds are migratory in winter.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类在冬天是迁徙的。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by migration; tending to migrate.

words.ex: The weather is mild today.
words.ex_cn: 今天天气温和。
words.en: Mild is used to describe something that is not extreme, severe, or strong, such as weather, taste, or behavior.

words.ex: The old book has mildew on its pages.
words.ex_cn: 那本旧书的书页上有霉菌。
words.en: Mildew is a type of fungus that grows on plants or on organic materials such as paper, leather, or cloth, especially in warm and damp conditions.

words.ex: He walks one mile to school every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天步行一英里去学校。
words.en: A unit of linear measure equal to 1,760 yards (approximately 1.609 kilometers).

words.ex: The car has high mileage.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车行驶的英里数很高。
words.en: Mileage refers to the distance traveled, measured in miles, or the benefits or advantages gained from a particular situation or activity.

words.ex: Graduating from high school was a big milestone for him.
words.ex_cn: 从高中毕业对他来说是一个重要的事件。
words.en: A milestone is a significant event or stage in the development of something.

words.tr:
adj. 激进的；好战的
n. 激进；好战
words.ex: He is a militant who protests every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个每天抗议的激进分子。
words.en: A militant person is someone who is engaged in warfare or combat, or who is aggressively active in a cause.

words.tr:
adj. 军事的；军用的；
n. 军队；武装力量；
words.ex: The military base is near the border.
words.ex_cn: 军事基地靠近边境。
words.en: relating to or characteristic of soldiers or armed forces

words.ex: The militia protected the village during the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 民兵在冲突期间保护了村庄。
words.en: A militia is a group of people who are not professional soldiers but who have military training and can act as an army.

words.ex: He drinks a glass of milk every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上喝一杯牛奶。
words.en: Milk is a white liquid produced by cows, goats, and some other animals, which people drink and use in cooking.

words.ex: The milkman delivers milk every morning.
words.ex_cn: 送奶工每天早上送牛奶。
words.en: A milkman is a person who delivers milk to people's homes.

words.ex: The milk looks milky and smooth.
words.ex_cn: 这牛奶看起来乳状且顺滑。
words.en: Resembling milk in color or consistency; containing milk.

words.ex: The old mill stands by the river.
words.ex_cn: 旧磨坊坐落在河边。
words.en: A mill is a building in which grain is crushed to make flour. It can also refer to a factory where certain materials are processed or manufactured.

words.ex: The millennium began in the year 2000.
words.ex_cn: 一千年始于2000年。
words.en: A millennium is a period of one thousand years.

words.ex: The miller ground wheat into flour every morning.
words.ex_cn: 磨坊主每天早上把小麦磨成面粉。
words.en: A miller is a person who owns or works in a mill, especially a grain mill.

words.ex: The worm is five millimetres long.
words.ex_cn: 这条虫子五毫米长。
words.en: A millimetre is a unit of length in the metric system, equal to one thousandth of a metre.

words.tr:
num. 一百万；
n. 百万；百万个；
words.ex: There are a million stars in the sky.
words.ex_cn: 天空中有百万颗星星。
words.en: A million is the number 1,000,000.

words.ex: He became a millionaire after selling his app.
words.ex_cn: 他卖掉自己的应用后成了百万富翁。
words.en: A millionaire is a person whose wealth amounts to a million or more in currency units such as dollars, pounds, or euros.

words.ex: The child mimics her mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿她妈妈的声音。
words.en: If someone or something mimics another person or thing, they try to be like them or copy their behavior or characteristics.

words.tr:
v. 切碎；剁碎；装腔作势地小步走
n. 绞碎的肉
words.ex: He minces garlic for the sauce.
words.ex_cn: 他把大蒜剁碎用来做酱。
words.en: To mince means to cut food, especially meat, into very small pieces, or to walk or speak in an affected manner.

words.tr: n. 碎肉器（等于 mincing machine）；说话吞吐的人; n. （Mincer）人名；（...
words.ex: She used a mincer to prepare the ground beef for the burgers.
words.ex_cn: 她用碎肉器准备汉堡用的牛肉馅。
words.en: A mincer is a machine which cuts meat into very small pieces by forcing it through very small holes.

words.tr:
n. 头脑；意向；心；智力；
v. 介意；注意；
words.ex: He lost his mind after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后失去了理智。
words.en: Your mind is your ability to think and reason. If you mind something, you are bothered by it or you object to it.

words.tr:
pron. 我的（东西）；
n. 矿；
v. 采矿；
words.ex: This book is mine.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是我的。
words.en: Used to refer to a thing or things belonging to or associated with the speaker. A place where minerals are extracted from the earth. To extract minerals from the earth.

words.ex: The miner works deep underground.
words.ex_cn: 矿工在地下深处工作。
words.en: A miner is a person who works in a mine, extracting coal, gold, or other minerals.

words.ex: Rock contains many minerals.
words.ex_cn: 岩石中含有许多矿物。
words.en: A mineral is a solid substance that occurs naturally and has a specific chemical composition and structure.

words.tr: v. 使相混；使联结；交际
words.ex: He mingled the two colors to make a new one.
words.ex_cn: 他把两种颜色混合在一起，创造出一种新颜色。
words.en: If things such as sounds, smells, or feelings mingle, they mix or combine with each other, or if people mingle, they talk to each other at a social event.

words.tr:
adj. 微型的；
n. 微型画；小型模型；
words.ex: He bought a miniature car for his collection.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的收藏买了一辆微型汽车。
words.en: A miniature is a very small detailed painting, often a portrait. It can also refer to a small-scale model or representation of something.

words.tr: n. [计] 小型计算机；微型电脑
words.ex: He uses a minicomputer for his science project.
words.ex_cn: 他用一台小型计算机做他的科学项目。
words.en: A minicomputer is a computer of a size intermediate between a microcomputer and a mainframe.

words.tr: adj. 最低限度的；极少的；最小的；
words.ex: He made minimal changes to the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对计划做了最低限度的修改。
words.en: Something that is minimal is very small in quantity, value, or degree.

words.tr: v. 减到最少；使最小化；
words.ex: Try to minimize waste in the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 尽量减少厨房里的浪费。
words.en: To minimize something means to reduce it to the smallest possible amount or degree.

words.tr:
n. 最小值；
adj. 最小量的；
words.ex: The minimum of the function is 5.
words.ex_cn: 这个函数的最小值是5。
words.en: The minimum is the smallest or least amount possible or allowed.

words.ex: The minister signed the new law.
words.ex_cn: 部长签署了新法律。
words.en: A minister is a person who is in charge of a particular government department or a member of the clergy in some Christian churches.

words.ex: The ministry of education controls schools.
words.ex_cn: 教育部管理学校。
words.en: A ministry is a government department, especially in Britain, which is responsible for a particular area of administration, such as health or education.

words.tr:
adj. 次要的；轻微的；小的；小调的；
n. 未成年人；
words.ex: The mistake was a minor error.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误是一个小错误。
words.en: A minor is a person who is under the age at which they legally become an adult.

words.ex: The minority group voted for change.
words.ex_cn: 少数群体投票支持变革。
words.en: A minority is a group of people within a community or country who are different from the majority of the people there in race, religion, or political beliefs.

words.ex: She added a mint leaf to her drink.
words.ex_cn: 她在饮料里加了一片薄荷叶。
words.en: Mint is a plant with fresh-tasting leaves. It is also the place where coins are made, or the act of making coins.

words.tr:
adj. 零下的；负的；
n. 缺点；
prep. 减去；
words.ex: The temperature is minus ten degrees Celsius.
words.ex_cn: 气温是零下十摄氏度。
words.en: A minus is a mathematical symbol that represents subtraction or a negative quantity.

words.tr:
n. 分钟；一会儿；
adj. 微小的；极小的；
words.ex: I waited for five minutes.
words.ex_cn: 我等了五分钟。
words.en: A minute is a unit of time equal to sixty seconds or a sixtieth of an hour.

words.ex: The child's recovery was a miracle.
words.ex_cn: 孩子的康复是个奇迹。
words.en: A miracle is an event that cannot be explained by the laws of nature and is therefore considered to be the work of a divine agency.

words.tr: adj. 奇迹般的；不可思议的；神奇的
words.ex: The sick boy made a miraculous recovery.
words.ex_cn: 那个生病的男孩奇迹般地康复了。
words.en: If you describe a good event as miraculous, you mean that it is very surprising and unexpected.

words.ex: He saw a mirage in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 他在沙漠中看到了海市蜃楼。
words.en: An optical illusion caused by atmospheric conditions, especially the appearance of a sheet of water in a desert or on a hot road caused by the refraction of light from the sky by heated air.

words.tr:
n. 泥潭；泥沼；困境
v. 使陷进泥坑里
words.ex: The car got stuck in the mire.
words.ex_cn: 汽车陷在泥沼里了。
words.en: Mire refers to an area of wet, soggy ground or a difficult situation from which it is hard to extricate oneself.

words.ex: She looked at herself in the mirror.
words.ex_cn: 她对着镜子看自己。
words.en: A mirror is a flat piece of glass which reflects light, so that when you look at it you can see yourself reflected in it.

words.ex: He did misappropriate the company's money.
words.ex_cn: 他确实挪用了公司的钱。
words.en: If someone misappropriates money or property that does not belong to them, they take it without permission and use it for their own purposes.

words.tr: n. 流产；早产；误投；失败
words.ex: She had a miscarriage last month.
words.ex_cn: 她上个月流产了。
words.en: A miscarriage is the premature expulsion of a fetus from the womb before it is able to survive independently, or a failure to achieve the intended result of a plan or action.

words.ex: She miscarried in the third month of pregnancy.
words.ex_cn: 她在怀孕第三个月时流产了。
words.en: To miscarry means to have a pregnancy end prematurely and not result in a live birth. It can also mean to fail to achieve an intended purpose or to be delivered to the wrong place.

words.ex: He bought some miscellaneous items at the store.
words.ex_cn: 他在商店里买了一些各种各样的东西。
words.en: Consisting of a variety of ingredients or parts.

words.ex: He lost his keys by a mischance.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心弄丢了钥匙。
words.en: An unlucky event or accident.

words.tr: n. 恶作剧；淘气；伤害；损害
words.ex: The boy caused mischief by letting the cats out.
words.ex_cn: 那个男孩放出了猫，惹了麻烦。
words.en: Mischief is behavior, especially by children, that is slightly bad but is not intended to cause serious harm or damage.

words.tr: v. 误解，误会；抱错误看法，未能理解；（尤指因误解而）拙劣判断，不周全的计划
words.ex: He often misconceives her intentions.
words.ex_cn: 他经常误解她的意图。
words.en: If you misconceive something, you misunderstand it or have a wrong idea about it.

words.ex: The boy was punished for his misdeed.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩因他的恶劣行为而受到惩罚。
words.en: A misdeed is a wrong or illegal deed; a crime or sin.

words.ex: The miser saved all his money and never spent it.
words.ex_cn: 这个吝啬鬼把所有的钱都存起来，从不花掉。
words.en: A miser is a person who is extremely unwilling to spend money, often to the point of living in poverty despite having wealth.

words.ex: He felt miserable after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到很悲惨。
words.en: If you are miserable, you are very unhappy.

words.ex: He felt deep misery after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到深深的痛苦。
words.en: Misery is a state of great unhappiness and emotional distress.

words.ex: He lost his job, which was a great misfortune.
words.ex_cn: 他丢了工作，这是一场巨大的不幸。
words.en: An unfortunate condition or event.

words.tr:
n. 疑虑；怀疑
v. 使疑虑；使担忧；“misgive”的现在分词
words.ex: He had a misgiving about the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个计划感到不安。
words.en: A misgiving is a feeling of doubt or anxiety about something that might happen or might have happened.

words.tr: adj. 错误的； v. “misguide”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: His misguided decision cost him his job.
words.ex_cn: 他错误的决定让他丢了工作。
words.en: If you describe an opinion or plan as misguided, you are critical of it because you think it is based on an incorrect idea or judgment.

words.tr: v. 处理不当；使用不当
words.ex: He mishandled the situation and made it worse.
words.ex_cn: 他处理不当，让情况变得更糟。
words.en: If you mishandle something, you deal with it badly or carelessly, often causing problems or damage.

words.tr: n. 不幸之事；灾祸；恶运
words.ex: He had a little mishap when he dropped his coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心把咖啡洒了，出了点小差错。
words.en: A mishap is an unlucky accident.

words.ex: He misinterprets her words as anger.
words.ex_cn: 他误解了她的话，以为是生气。
words.en: To interpret wrongly; misunderstand.

words.ex: He misleads his friends with false stories.
words.ex_cn: 他用虚假的故事误导他的朋友。
words.en: If you say that someone has misled you, you mean that they have made you believe something which is not true, either by telling you a lie or by giving you a wrong idea or impression.

words.tr: v. 歪曲；不实报道；曲解
words.ex: He misrepresents the facts to win the debate.
words.ex_cn: 他歪曲事实以赢得辩论。
words.en: To give a false or misleading account of the nature of something.

words.tr:
v. 错过；想念；漏掉；
n. 小姐；
words.ex: I missed the bus this morning.
words.ex_cn: 我今天早上错过了公交车。
words.en: To fail to hit, reach, catch, or otherwise make contact with something; to feel the absence or loss of someone or something.

words.ex: The army launched a missile at the target.
words.ex_cn: 军队向目标发射了一枚导弹。
words.en: A missile is a weapon that is sent through the air and that explodes when it hits the thing it is aimed at.

words.tr: adj. 失去的；失踪的； v. 错失；“miss”的现在分词；
words.ex: The missing book was found under the bed.
words.ex_cn: 那本丢失的书在床下找到了。
words.en: If someone or something is missing, they are not in their usual place, and you cannot find them.

words.ex: His mission is to help poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他的使命是帮助贫困儿童。
words.en: A mission is an important task that people are given to do, especially one that involves travelling to another country.

words.ex: The missionary taught children in a small village.
words.ex_cn: 这位传教士在一个小村庄里教孩子们。
words.en: A missionary is a person who is sent to a foreign country to spread a religion.

words.ex: There was a thin mist over the lake at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 黎明时分，湖面上有一层薄雾。
words.en: Mist is a thin layer of cloud that touches the ground. It is less dense than fog and can make it difficult to see clearly.

words.ex: He made a mistake in his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他在作业中犯了一个错误。
words.en: If you make a mistake, you do something which you did not intend to do, or which produces a result that you do not want.

words.tr: adj. 搞错的；弄错的；误解的； v. “mistake”的过去分词；
words.ex: He was mistaken about the time of the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他对会议的时间搞错了。
words.en: If you are mistaken about something, you are wrong about it.

words.ex: Mister Brown is my teacher.
words.ex_cn: 布朗先生是我的老师。
words.en: A title used before a man's name or position to address or refer to him politely.

words.tr: n. 女主人；情妇；女教师（英）
words.ex: The mistress of the house welcomed the guests warmly.
words.ex_cn: 女主人热情地欢迎了客人。
words.en: A woman who has control or authority over others, especially a woman who is in charge of a household or institution.

words.ex: The morning was misty and quiet.
words.ex_cn: 早晨雾蒙蒙的，很安静。
words.en: If the weather is misty, there is mist in the air that makes it difficult to see far.

words.ex: He misunderstands the instructions.
words.ex_cn: 他误解了这些说明。
words.en: If you misunderstand someone or something, you do not understand them properly.

words.tr: n. 误解；误会； v. “misunderstand”的现在分词；
words.ex: There was a misunderstanding between them about the time.
words.ex_cn: 他们之间对时间产生了误解。
words.en: A misunderstanding is a failure to understand something correctly, often leading to confusion or disagreement.

words.tr:
v. 滥用；误用；虐待
n. 滥用；误用；虐待
words.ex: He misuses his phone during class.
words.ex_cn: 他在上课时滥用手机。
words.en: The incorrect or improper use of something.

words.ex: Planting trees can mitigate air pollution.
words.ex_cn: 植树可以减轻空气污染。
words.en: To mitigate something means to make it less unpleasant, serious, or painful.

words.ex: He wears a mitten to keep his hand warm.
words.ex_cn: 他戴一只连指手套来暖手。
words.en: A mitten is a glove that has one section for the thumb and another section for all four fingers together, used to keep the hands warm in cold weather.

words.tr:
n. 混合；结合；
v. 混合；掺入；合成；交往；
words.ex: The recipe calls for a mix of flour and sugar.
words.ex_cn: 这个食谱需要一种面粉和糖的混合物。
words.en: To combine two or more substances so that they become a single substance, or to be combined in this way.

words.ex: She used a mixer to make the cake batter.
words.ex_cn: 她用搅拌器来做蛋糕面糊。
words.en: A mixer is a machine or device used for mixing things together, especially in cooking or in music production.

words.ex: The recipe calls for a mixture of flour and water.
words.ex_cn: 这个食谱需要一种面粉和水的混合物。
words.en: A mixture is a substance made by combining other substances together.

words.tr:
v. 呻吟；呼啸；抱怨
n. 呻吟声；萧萧声；抱怨
words.ex: He moans when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 他累了的时候会呻吟。
words.en: If you moan, you make a low sound, usually because you are unhappy or in pain.

words.ex: The mob broke the windows and shouted loudly.
words.ex_cn: 乌合之众砸了窗户并大声喊叫。
words.en: A mob is a large crowd of people, especially one that is disorderly and intent on causing trouble or violence.

words.ex: The mobile table can be moved easily.
words.ex_cn: 这个可移动的桌子很容易搬动。
words.en: A mobile is something that can move or be moved easily.

words.ex: The government will mobilize troops to help after the earthquake.
words.ex_cn: 政府将调动军队在地震后提供帮助。
words.en: If you mobilize a group of people, or if they mobilize, they prepare to take action, especially in a military context.

words.tr:
v. 嘲笑；嘲弄；
adj. 仿制的；
words.ex: They mock him for his accent.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他口音而嘲笑他。
words.en: To mock someone means to laugh at them, tease them, or make them look foolish, often by imitating their behavior or speech.

words.ex: The mode of transportation is a bike.
words.ex_cn: 出行的方式是骑自行车。
words.en: A mode is a particular way or style in which something is done or experienced.

words.tr:
n. 模型；模特；模范；型号；
v. 将…做成模型；当模特；
words.ex: The architect built a model of the new building.
words.ex_cn: 建筑师制作了新大楼的模型。
words.en: A model is a person whose job is to wear and show new styles of clothes and other products, or a representation of something, often on a smaller scale, or a particular design or type of product.

words.ex: He ate a moderate amount of food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了适量的食物。
words.en: If you moderate something or if it moderates, it becomes less extreme or violent, or if you moderate a discussion, you help the people in it to reach an agreement.

words.tr: adv. 适度地；不过分地；有节制地；
words.ex: He eats moderately to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他适度饮食以保持健康。
words.en: In a manner that is neither too much nor too little; to a moderate extent.

words.ex: This house has a modern design.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子具有现代的设计。
words.en: Modern means relating to the present time, for example the present decade or present century.

words.ex: The country is working on modernization of its roads.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正在努力改善其道路的现代化。
words.en: Modernization is the process of making something modern and more suited to present-day needs.

words.ex: The city plans to modernize its old subway system.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市计划现代化其老旧的地铁系统。
words.en: To modernize something means to change it so that it is more modern, for example by using more recent technology or methods.

words.tr: adj. 不多的；适度的；谦虚的；
words.ex: He made a modest profit last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年的利润不多。
words.en: If you say that someone is modest, you approve of them because they do not talk much about their abilities or achievements.

words.ex: His modesty made everyone like him.
words.ex_cn: 他的谦虚让所有人都喜欢他。
words.en: Modesty is the quality of not being too proud or confident about yourself or your abilities.

words.ex: The modification improved the design.
words.ex_cn: 这个修改改进了设计。
words.en: A modification is a change or alteration made to something to improve it or to make it suitable for a different purpose.

words.tr: adj. 改良的；改进的；修正的； v. 更改；修饰；“modify”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The modified version works better than the old one.
words.ex_cn: 改良后的版本比旧版本更好用。
words.en: Changed in form or character.

words.ex: He will modify the plan tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会更改计划。
words.en: To change something slightly, especially in order to make it more suitable for a particular purpose.

words.ex: She wears modish clothes every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天穿时髦的衣服。
words.en: If something is modish, it is fashionable and modern.

words.ex: He modulates his voice to sound calm.
words.ex_cn: 他调节自己的声音以显得平静。
words.en: To modulate means to change or adjust something, such as your voice or a piece of equipment, to achieve a desired effect or to make it suitable for a particular situation.

words.ex: The software has five different modules.
words.ex_cn: 这个软件有五个不同的模块。
words.en: A module is one of the separate parts of a course of study, especially at a college or university.

words.ex: The soil is moist after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后土壤是潮湿的。
words.en: Slightly wet; damp or humid.

words.ex: The soil has too much moisture.
words.ex_cn: 土壤中有太多湿气。
words.en: Moisture is tiny drops of water in the air, on a surface, or in a substance, that make it feel wet.

words.ex: The baker used a metal mold to shape the cake.
words.ex_cn: 面包师用一个金属模具来塑造蛋糕。
words.en: A mold is a hollow container used to give shape to molten or hot liquid material when it cools and hardens. It can also refer to a fungus that grows on food or damp surfaces.

words.ex: The mole dug a tunnel under the garden.
words.ex_cn: 鼹鼠在花园下挖了一条隧道。
words.en: A mole is a small animal with black fur that lives underground. It can also refer to a small dark spot on the skin or a person who secretly gives information to an enemy.

words.tr: adj. 分子的；分子构成的；
words.ex: Water is a molecular compound.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种分子化合物。
words.en: Relating to or consisting of molecules.

words.ex: Water is made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom in a molecule.
words.ex_cn: 水由两个氢原子和一个氧原子组成一个分子。
words.en: A molecule is the smallest particle in a chemical element or compound that has the chemical properties of that element or compound. Molecules are made up of atoms that are held together by chemical bonds.

words.ex: He was arrested for molesting a child.
words.ex_cn: 他因骚扰儿童而被逮捕。
words.en: To molest someone means to assault or harass them, especially sexually.

words.ex: The molten lava flowed down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 熔化的岩浆从山上流下。
words.en: Molten is used to describe substances that have been heated to a very high temperature and have turned into a liquid.

words.ex: He waited for a moment before speaking.
words.ex_cn: 他等了一会儿才开口。
words.en: A moment is a very short period of time.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的；瞬间的；刹那间的
words.ex: The light made a momentary flash.
words.ex_cn: 灯光闪了一下，但只持续了一瞬间。
words.en: lasting for a very short time

words.ex: The momentous decision changed his life.
words.ex_cn: 这个重要的决定改变了他的一生。
words.en: If you refer to a decision, event, or change as momentous, you mean that it is very important, often because of the effects that it will have in the future.

words.ex: The team gained momentum after scoring the first goal.
words.ex_cn: 球队在进第一个球后获得了势头。
words.en: Momentum is the ability of something to keep increasing, developing, or being more successful.

words.ex: The monarch ruled the country for 50 years.
words.ex_cn: 这位君主统治这个国家长达50年。
words.en: A monarch is a king, queen, emperor, or empress.

words.ex: The country still has a monarchy with a king as the head of state.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家仍然实行君主制，国王是国家元首。
words.en: A monarchy is a form of government in which a country is ruled by a monarch, such as a king or queen.

words.ex: The monks live in a quiet monastery.
words.ex_cn: 僧侣们住在一座安静的修道院里。
words.en: A monastery is a building or collection of buildings in which monks live and work.

words.ex: I have a meeting on Monday.
words.ex_cn: 我星期一有个会议。
words.en: Monday is the day of the week between Sunday and Tuesday.

words.ex: The monetary policy affects prices.
words.ex_cn: 货币政策影响价格。
words.en: Monetary means relating to money, especially the total amount of money in a country.

words.ex: I need the money for the bill.
words.ex_cn: 我需要这笔钱来付账单。
words.en: Money is the coins or bank notes that you use to buy things, or the amount of these that you have.

words.ex: The teacher monitors the students' progress each week.
words.ex_cn: 老师每周监控学生的进步。
words.en: A monitor is a machine that is used to check or record things, for example in a factory or hospital. In a school, a monitor is a student who helps the teacher with various duties.

words.ex: The monk meditates every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这位僧侣每天早上冥想。
words.en: A monk is a member of a religious community of men who live by certain vows and usually wear a habit.

words.ex: The monkey is eating a banana.
words.ex_cn: 猴子正在吃一根香蕉。
words.en: A monkey is a small to medium-sized primate that typically has a long tail, most kinds of which live in trees in tropical countries.

words.tr: n. 独白；独角戏；长篇大论
words.ex: He gave a monologue on stage.
words.ex_cn: 他在舞台上发表了一段独白。
words.en: A monologue is a long speech by one person, especially in a play or film, or a long speech by one person during a conversation.

words.ex: The big company tries to monopolize the market.
words.ex_cn: 这家大公司试图垄断市场。
words.en: If a company or person monopolizes something, they have complete control over it, so that other people cannot share it.

words.ex: He has a monopoly on selling ice cream in this town.
words.ex_cn: 他在这座小镇上垄断了冰淇淋的销售。
words.en: If a company, person, or state has a monopoly on something such as an industry, they have complete control over it, so that it is impossible for others to become involved in it.

words.tr: adj. 单调乏味的；毫无变化的；
words.ex: The work is monotonous and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作单调乏味。
words.en: Something that is monotonous is very boring because it has a regular, repeated pattern which never changes.

words.tr: n. 单调；枯燥；千篇一律
words.ex: He felt bored because of the monotony of his daily work.
words.ex_cn: 他因为日常工作的单调而感到无聊。
words.en: If you refer to the monotony of something, you are criticizing it because it is boring and has no variety.

words.ex: The monsoon brings heavy rain to India each summer.
words.ex_cn: 季风每年夏天给印度带来大雨。
words.en: A monsoon is a seasonal wind in South and Southeast Asia, blowing from the southwest between May and September and bringing rain (the wet monsoon), or from the northeast between October and April (the dry monsoon).

words.ex: The old ship was a monster on the sea.
words.ex_cn: 那艘旧船在海上是个庞然大物。
words.en: A monster is an imaginary creature that is very large, ugly, and frightening.

words.ex: The monster made a monstrous sound.
words.ex_cn: 这个怪物发出了巨大的声音。
words.en: If you describe something as monstrous, you mean that it is extremely large or that it is extremely unpleasant or wrong.

words.ex: He will return next month.
words.ex_cn: 他下个月回来。
words.en: A month is one of the twelve periods of time that a year is divided into, for example January or February.

words.tr:
adj. 每月的；每月一次的；
n. 月刊；
adv. 每月一次；每个月；
words.ex: He pays his rent monthly.
words.ex_cn: 他每月支付房租。
words.en: Monthly means happening or done once a month or every month.

words.tr: n. 历史遗迹；纪念碑；不朽作品；
words.ex: The ancient monument attracts many tourists each year.
words.ex_cn: 这座古代历史遗迹每年吸引许多游客。
words.en: A monument is a large structure, usually made of stone, which is built to remind people of an important person or event.

words.ex: The project was a monumental task.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目是一项巨大的任务。
words.en: If you describe something as monumental, you are emphasizing that it is very large and impressive, or that it is of great importance or significance.

words.ex: His mood changed after he heard the good news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个好消息后，心情变了。
words.en: A mood is a temporary state of mind or feeling.

words.ex: The moon shines brightly in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 月亮在夜空中明亮地照耀。
words.en: The natural satellite of the earth, visible (chiefly at night) by reflected light from the sun.

words.tr:
n. 月光
v. 兼职；（尤在夜间）从事第二职业
words.ex: She works as a waitress at night to moonlight.
words.ex_cn: 她晚上当服务员来兼职。
words.en: The light that comes from the moon at night.

words.tr:
n. 夜间活动；夜袭；（尤在夜间）从事第二职业
v. 兼职；（尤在夜间）从事第二职业；“moonlight”的现在分词】
words.ex: He has moonlighting as a taxi driver after his day job.
words.ex_cn: 他在白天工作之后，晚上开出租车。
words.en: Moonlighting refers to the practice of working at an extra job, especially without telling your main employer.

words.tr:
n. 旷野地；荒野；高沼
v. （使）停泊；系泊
words.ex: The sheep graze on the moor near the village.
words.ex_cn: 羊在村庄附近的旷野地上吃草。
words.en: A moor is an area of open land, often with poor soil, that is covered with grass, heather, and low bushes. It can also refer to the act of securing a ship or boat to a fixed object or the land.

words.ex: He had a mop of curly hair that always looked messy.
words.ex_cn: 他有一头乱蓬蓬的卷发，总是看起来很凌乱。
words.en: A mop is a tool for cleaning floors, consisting of a bundle of thick strings or a sponge attached to a long handle. As a verb, it means to clean or wipe something with a mop.

words.tr: n. 摩托自行车 v. <贬>忧郁地闲荡( mope的过去式和过去分词 )
words.ex: He rode his moped to the park.
words.ex_cn: 他骑着他的摩托自行车去公园。
words.en: A moped is a small motorcycle which you can also pedal like a bicycle.

words.tr:
adj. 道德的；道义上的；
n. 寓意；
words.ex: It is a moral duty to tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 说实话是一种道德责任。
words.en: Concerned with the principles of right and wrong behavior and the goodness or badness of human character.

words.ex: The team's morale improved after they won the game.
words.ex_cn: 球队赢了比赛后，士气提升了。
words.en: Morale is the amount of confidence and cheerfulness that a group of people have.

words.ex: He always follows his morality in daily life.
words.ex_cn: 他日常生活中总是遵循自己的道德。
words.en: Morality is the belief that some behaviour is right and acceptable and that other behaviour is wrong.

words.tr: adj. 病态的；心理不健康的
words.ex: He has a morbid fear of the dark.
words.ex_cn: 他对黑暗有一种病态的恐惧。
words.en: If you describe a person or their interest in something as morbid, you mean that they are very interested in unpleasant things, especially death, and you think this is strange.

words.tr:
adv. 更加；
adj. 更多的；
pron. 更多的人或物；
words.ex: She wants to learn more about science.
words.ex_cn: 她想更深入了解科学。
words.en: You use 'more' to indicate that there is a greater amount of something than before or than average, or than something else. You can use 'more' with a noun to indicate that there is a greater amount of it than before or than average, or than something else.

words.ex: He likes reading books; moreover, he writes his own stories.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢读书；此外，他还写自己的故事。
words.en: You use moreover to introduce a piece of information that adds to or supports the previous statement.

words.ex: I drink coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 我每天早晨喝咖啡。
words.en: The morning is the part of each day between the time that people usually wake up and the time they start work or school, or the part of the day before noon.

words.tr:
n. 凡人
adj. 致命的；终有一死的
words.ex: All mortal beings must die someday.
words.ex_cn: 所有凡人都终有一死。
words.en: If you refer to the fact that people are mortal, you mean that they have to die and cannot live forever.

words.ex: He took out a mortgage to buy his first house.
words.ex_cn: 他申请了一笔抵押贷款来购买他的第一套房子。
words.en: A mortgage is a loan of money which you get from a bank or building society in order to buy a house.

words.ex: The floor has a colorful mosaic of flowers.
words.ex_cn: 地板上有一个五彩的花卉镶嵌图案。
words.en: A mosaic is a picture or pattern produced by arranging together small colored pieces of hard material, such as stone, tile, or glass.

words.tr:
n. 穆斯林；伊斯兰教信徒
adj. 穆斯林的；伊斯兰教的
words.ex: He is a moslem who prays five times a day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名每天祈祷五次的穆斯林。
words.en: A Moslem is a follower of the religion of Islam.

words.ex: He goes to the mosque every Friday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周五去清真寺。
words.en: A mosque is a building where Muslims go to worship.

words.ex: A mosquito bit my arm last night.
words.ex_cn: 一只蚊子昨晚咬了我的胳膊。
words.en: A mosquito is a small flying insect that bites people and animals in order to feed on their blood. Some mosquitoes can transmit diseases.

words.ex: The stone is covered with green moss.
words.ex_cn: 石头上覆盖着绿色的苔藓。
words.en: Moss is a small, green plant that grows in damp, shady places, often forming a soft, thick layer on the ground, trees, or rocks.

words.tr:
adv. 最；
pron. 大部分；
adj. 最多的；大多数的；
words.ex: He is most tired after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后最累。
words.en: You use most to refer to the majority of a group of things or people or the largest part of something.

words.ex: He is mostly late for class.
words.ex_cn: 他主要迟到上课。
words.en: You use mostly to indicate that a statement is generally true, for example true about most of a group of things or people, true most of the time, or true in most situations.

words.ex: They stayed at a motel near the highway.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在高速公路旁的一家汽车旅馆。
words.en: A motel is a hotel which is designed for people who are travelling by car, usually with parking spaces next to each room.

words.ex: A moth flew into the room through the window.
words.ex_cn: 一只蛾子从窗户飞进了房间。
words.en: A moth is an insect with wings that is related to the butterfly. Moths are often attracted to light and are mostly active at night.

words.ex: My mother cooks dinner every evening.
words.ex_cn: 我妈妈每天晚上做晚饭。
words.en: A mother is a female parent of a child. Mothers are women who inhabit or perform the role of bearing some relation to their children, who may or may not be their biological offspring.

words.ex: My mother-in-law lives next door.
words.ex_cn: 我的岳母住在隔壁。
words.en: The mother of one's spouse.

words.ex: The motif of love appears in many poems.
words.ex_cn: 爱的主题出现在许多诗歌中。
words.en: A motif is a design or pattern that is used in a piece of art or music, or a theme that is repeated in a work of literature.

words.ex: The motion of the ball is very fast.
words.ex_cn: 球的运动非常快。
words.en: The action or process of moving or being moved.

words.ex: The cat sat motionless by the window.
words.ex_cn: 猫静静地坐在窗边。
words.en: If someone or something is motionless, they are not moving at all.

words.ex: Good teachers motivate students to learn.
words.ex_cn: 好老师激励学生学习。
words.en: To motivate someone means to provide them with a reason for doing something, especially something that requires effort.

words.ex: His motivation is to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他的动机是帮助他人。
words.en: Motivation is the enthusiasm or reason for doing something.

words.ex: His motive was to help his family.
words.ex_cn: 他的动机是帮助家人。
words.en: Your motive for doing something is your reason for doing it.

words.tr: n. 马达；发动机；机动车；
words.ex: The car has a strong motor.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车有一个强大的马达。
words.en: A motor is a device that changes energy into mechanical motion, especially such a device that provides power for a vehicle or for another device with moving parts.

words.ex: He drives a motorcar to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天开车去上班。
words.en: A motorcar is a road vehicle, usually with four wheels, powered by an internal combustion engine or electric motor, and designed to carry a small number of people.

words.ex: He rides a motorcycle to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天骑摩托车去上班。
words.en: A motorcycle is a vehicle with two wheels and an engine.

words.ex: The motorist stopped at the red light.
words.ex_cn: 这位驾车者在红灯前停下了车。
words.en: A motorist is a person who drives a car.

words.ex: He drives on the motorway every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都在高速公路上开车。
words.en: A motorway is a wide road specially built for fast travel over long distances, with a limited number of places at which drivers can enter and leave it.

words.ex: Her motto is 'Never give up.'
words.ex_cn: 她的座右铭是‘永不放弃’。
words.en: A motto is a short sentence or phrase that expresses a rule for sensible behavior, especially a way of behaving in a particular situation.

words.tr:
n. 模具；霉；
v. 铸造；
words.ex: The clay was poured into the mould to shape the pot.
words.ex_cn: 将黏土倒入模具中以塑造花盆。
words.en: A mould is a hollow container that you pour a liquid or soft substance into, which then becomes solid in the same shape as the container. Mould can also refer to a fungus that grows on old food or on damp surfaces.

words.tr:
n. 山；
v. 逐渐增加；
words.ex: He climbed the mount early in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 他一大早爬了那座山。
words.en: To mount something means to go up it or to get on it. It can also refer to the act of organizing and beginning something, such as an event or an exhibition.

words.tr: n. 山；山脉；一大堆；大量；
words.ex: He climbed a tall mountain last summer.
words.ex_cn: 去年夏天，他爬了一座高山。
words.en: A mountain is a very high area of land with steep sides, much higher than a hill.

words.ex: The mountainous region has many hiking trails.
words.ex_cn: 这个多山的地区有许多徒步小径。
words.en: A mountainous area has a lot of mountains.

words.ex: She mourns her dog every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天都在哀悼她的狗。
words.en: To feel or express deep sorrow or regret for someone or something.

words.ex: He sang a mournful song at the funeral.
words.ex_cn: 他在葬礼上唱了一首悲伤的歌。
words.en: If you are mournful, you are very sad.

words.tr:
n. 哀悼；悲痛；服丧
v. 悼念；哀痛；“mourn”的现在分词
words.ex: He is mourning the loss of his dog.
words.ex_cn: 他正在为失去他的狗而哀悼。
words.en: Mourning is the expression of deep sorrow for someone who has died, typically involving following certain conventions such as wearing black clothes.

words.ex: The mouse ran under the table.
words.ex_cn: 老鼠跑到了桌子下面。
words.en: A mouse is a small animal with a long tail, which is found in houses and fields and is often kept as a pet. In computing, a mouse is a small device that you move across a surface in order to move a cursor on your computer screen.

words.ex: He has a black moustache.
words.ex_cn: 他有一撮黑色的胡子。
words.en: A moustache is the hair that grows on a man's upper lip.

words.ex: He washed his mouth after eating.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完饭后洗了嘴。
words.en: The opening in the lower part of the human face used for speaking, eating, and breathing.

words.ex: He took a mouthful of soup.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了一口汤。
words.en: A mouthful is an amount of food or drink that you put into your mouth at one time.

words.tr:
v. 移动；搬家；
n. 行动；移动；
words.ex: Please move the chair.
words.ex_cn: 请移动椅子。
words.en: To change position or to cause something or someone to change position, especially in a particular direction or to a particular place.

words.tr: n. 运动；动作；活动；乐章；
words.ex: The movement of the sun changes the shadow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳的运动改变了影子。
words.en: The act or process of moving or being moved; a change of position or place.

words.ex: He watches a movie every Friday night.
words.ex_cn: 他每周五晚上都看电影。
words.en: A movie is a story or event recorded by a camera as a set of moving images and shown in a cinema or on television.

words.ex: Mr. Smith is my neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 史密斯先生是我的邻居。
words.en: A title used before a man's name or position to address or refer to him politely.

words.ex: Mrs. Brown teaches English at the school.
words.ex_cn: 布朗夫人在学校教英语。
words.en: A title used before a married woman's surname or full name.

words.ex: Ms. Li teaches English at our school.
words.ex_cn: 李老师在我们学校教英语。
words.en: a title used before the name of a woman regardless of her marital status

words.tr:
adv. 非常地；
adj. 多；许多；
pron. 许多；
words.ex: She is much happier now.
words.ex_cn: 她现在快乐多了。
words.en: A large amount or to a great degree.

words.ex: He has a lot of mucous in his nose.
words.ex_cn: 他的鼻子有很多黏液。
words.en: Relating to, producing, or resembling mucus.

words.ex: The dog ran through the mud.
words.ex_cn: 狗跑过了泥地。
words.en: Mud is a sticky mixture of earth and water.

words.tr:
v. 使混乱；使糊涂；胡乱应付
n. 混乱；糊涂
words.ex: He muddled the instructions and got confused.
words.ex_cn: 他把说明搞混了，感到困惑。
words.en: If you muddle things or people, you get them mixed up, so that you do not know which is which.

words.tr: adj. 泥泞的；模糊不清的；
words.ex: The road became muddy after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，这条路变得泥泞。
words.en: If something is muddy, it is covered in mud or full of mud. If you muddy something, you make it muddy or you make it less clear or more complicated.

words.tr: v. 使声音降低；压抑（声音）；蒙住；裹
words.ex: He muffled his laugh with a pillow.
words.ex_cn: 他用枕头捂住笑声。
words.en: To muffle a sound is to make it quieter or less clear, often by covering it or wrapping it in something.

words.ex: He wore a wool muffler in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他在冬天戴了一条羊毛围巾。
words.en: A muffler is a piece of cloth worn around the neck for warmth or a device used to reduce the noise emitted by an engine.

words.ex: He drank coffee from a large mug.
words.ex_cn: 他从一个大杯子里喝咖啡。
words.en: A mug is a large, deep cup with straight sides and a handle, used for hot drinks. It can also refer to someone's face or a foolish person. As a verb, it means to attack and rob someone violently in a public place.

words.tr: n. 骡子；顽固的人；拖鞋
words.ex: The farmer uses a mule to carry heavy boxes.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用骡子搬运沉重的箱子。
words.en: A mule is the offspring of a male donkey and a female horse. Mules are known for their strength and stubbornness.

words.tr: adj. 多种的；各式各样的
words.ex: She has multifarious hobbies, like painting, singing, and gardening.
words.ex_cn: 她有很多不同的爱好，比如绘画、唱歌和园艺。
words.en: If you describe things as multifarious, you mean that they are many and of various types.

words.ex: This is a multifunction tool that can cut, screw, and drill.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个多功能工具，可以切割、拧螺丝和钻孔。
words.en: Having or able to perform many functions.

words.tr: adj. 多边的；多国参加的
words.ex: The multilateral agreement helped many countries work together.
words.ex_cn: 这个多边协议帮助许多国家共同合作。
words.en: Involving or agreed upon by three or more parties, especially the governments of different countries.

words.ex: The store offers multiple flavors of ice cream.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店提供多种口味的冰淇淋。
words.en: If something is multiple, it consists of or involves many things of the same kind.

words.ex: He learned multiplication in second grade.
words.ex_cn: 他在二年级学习了乘法。
words.en: Multiplication is the process of calculating the total of one number multiplied by another.

words.ex: The bacteria multiply quickly.
words.ex_cn: 细菌迅速增加。
words.en: If you multiply one number by another, you add the first number to itself as many times as is indicated by the second number. For example, 2 multiplied by 3 is equal to 6.

words.ex: A multitude of people attended the festival.
words.ex_cn: 大量的人参加了这个节日。
words.en: A multitude of things or people is a very large number of them.

words.tr:
v. 咕哝；含糊地说
n. 含糊的话；咕哝
words.ex: He mumbles when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，他会嘟囔。
words.en: If you mumble, you speak very quietly and not at all clearly with the result that the words are difficult to understand.

words.ex: He had mumps last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周得了腮腺炎。
words.en: Mumps is a contagious disease that causes swelling of the salivary glands and can lead to more serious complications.

words.ex: His daily routine is mundane and boring.
words.ex_cn: 他的日常生活平凡而无聊。
words.en: Something that is mundane is very ordinary and not at all interesting or unusual.

words.ex: The municipal library is open every day.
words.ex_cn: 这座市政图书馆每天都开放。
words.en: Relating to a city or town or its governing body.

words.ex: The murder happened last night in the park.
words.ex_cn: 这起谋杀发生在昨晚的公园里。
words.en: Murder is the unlawful premeditated killing of one human being by another.

words.ex: The murderer was caught by the police.
words.ex_cn: 杀人犯被警察抓住了。
words.en: A murderer is a person who has committed the crime of murder.

words.tr:
n. 低语声；嘟哝
v. 低语；咕哝；私下抱怨
words.ex: I heard a murmur from the next room.
words.ex_cn: 我听到隔壁房间传来低语声。
words.en: A murmur is a low, indistinct, continuous sound, as of a stream or of voices.

words.ex: He strengthened his muscle by lifting weights.
words.ex_cn: 他通过举重来增强肌肉。
words.en: Muscle is the tissue in the body that can contract to produce movement or maintain the position of parts of the body.

words.tr: adj. 肌肉的；肌肉发达的；
words.ex: He has a muscular arm from lifting weights.
words.ex_cn: 他因为举重而拥有强壮的手臂。
words.en: Relating to or affecting the muscles; having well-developed muscles.

words.tr:
v. 沉思
n. （作家、画家等的）灵感；缪斯
words.ex: He often muses about the meaning of life.
words.ex_cn: 他常常沉思生命的意义。
words.en: In Greek mythology, the Muses are the goddesses of the inspiration of literature, science and the arts. As a verb, to muse means to think about something carefully and for a long time.

words.ex: We visited a museum last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 我们上周末参观了一个博物馆。
words.en: A museum is a building where a large number of interesting and valuable objects, such as works of art or historical items, are kept, studied, and displayed to the public.

words.ex: He picked a wild mushroom in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他在森林里摘了一朵野生蘑菇。
words.en: A mushroom is a fungus that grows in damp, dark places and has a stem with a rounded top.

words.ex: He loves listening to music every night.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢每天晚上听音乐。
words.en: Music is the pattern of sounds produced by people singing or playing instruments.

words.tr:
adj. 音乐的；擅长音乐的；
n. 音乐剧；音乐歌舞片；
words.ex: He loves musical songs.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢音乐的歌曲。
words.en: Relating to music; having the pleasant sound of music.

words.ex: He is a musician who plays the guitar.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位弹吉他的音乐家。
words.en: A musician is a person who plays a musical instrument, especially as a profession, or is musically talented.

words.tr:
auxv. 必须；一定要；
n. 必须做的事；必不可少的事物；
words.ex: You must finish your homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 你必须在晚饭前完成作业。
words.en: Used to indicate that something is very likely or certain to be true or to happen.

words.ex: He put mustard on his sandwich.
words.ex_cn: 他在三明治上加了芥末。
words.en: A pungent yellow or brown paste made from the ground seeds of certain plants, used as a condiment.

words.tr:
v. 鼓起；集合；召集
n. 集合；集合的人群
words.ex: He must muster courage to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他必须鼓起勇气在公众面前发言。
words.en: To muster means to gather or assemble (troops, etc.), especially for inspection or in preparation for battle. It can also mean to summon up (a feeling, attitude, or response).

words.ex: The mutation caused the plant to grow differently.
words.ex_cn: 这种突变使植物的生长方式发生了变化。
words.en: A mutation is a change in the structure of the genes of an organism that results in a variant form which may be transmitted to subsequent generations, caused by the alteration of single base units in DNA, or the deletion, insertion, or rearrangement of larger sections of genes or chromosomes.

words.tr:
adj. 哑的；无声的
n. 哑巴；沉默的人
v. 减弱…的声音
words.ex: He stayed mute during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议期间保持沉默。
words.en: If someone is mute, they are unable to speak.

words.tr:
v. 咕哝地抱怨；嘀咕
n. 咕哝地抱怨；嘀咕
words.ex: He mutters under his breath when he is angry.
words.ex_cn: 当他生气时，他会低声嘟囔。
words.en: To speak or say something in a low voice that is hard to hear, often because you are annoyed or complaining.

words.ex: He eats mutton for dinner every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日吃羊肉当晚餐。
words.en: Mutton is the meat of an adult sheep eaten as food.

words.ex: They have mutual respect for each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们彼此相互尊重。
words.en: Mutual is used to describe a situation, feeling, or action that is experienced, felt, or done by each of two or more parties towards the other or others.

words.ex: My book is on the table.
words.ex_cn: 我的书在桌子上。
words.en: Used to refer to oneself as the possessor of something.

words.tr:
adj. 无数的；
n. 无数；
words.ex: There are myriad stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有无数的星星。
words.en: A myriad of things or people is a very large number of them.

words.ex: I did it myself.
words.ex_cn: 我自己做的。
words.en: Used by a speaker to refer to himself or herself as the object of a verb or preposition when he or she is the subject of the clause.

words.ex: The mysterious box appeared on his doorstep.
words.ex_cn: 那个神秘的盒子出现在他的门口。
words.en: If someone or something is mysterious, it is not fully understood or explained and seems interesting or puzzling.

words.tr: n. 谜；难以理解的事物；
words.ex: The mystery of the missing key puzzled everyone.
words.ex_cn: 丢失的钥匙这个谜题让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: Something that is difficult or impossible to understand or explain.

words.tr:
adj. 神秘的；神秘主义的
n. 神秘主义者
words.ex: He saw a mystic light in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他在森林里看到一道神秘的光。
words.en: A mystic is a person who seeks by contemplation and self-surrender to obtain unity with or absorption into the Deity or the absolute, or who believes in the spiritual apprehension of truths that are beyond the intellect.

words.tr: v. 迷惑；使迷惑不解；使糊涂
words.ex: The magic trick will mystify the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术会让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If you are mystified by something, you find it impossible to explain or understand.

words.ex: It's a myth that eating late at night causes weight gain.
words.ex_cn: 晚上吃东西会导致发胖，这是一种错误观念。
words.en: A myth is a traditional story, especially one concerning the early history of a people or explaining some natural or social phenomenon, and typically involving supernatural beings or events.

words.ex: The dragon is a mythical creature.
words.ex_cn: 龙是一种神话中的生物。
words.en: Something that is mythical exists only in myths and is therefore imaginary.

words.tr: n. 神话；神话学；神话集；
words.ex: He loves reading Greek mythology.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢读希腊神话。
words.en: Mythology is a collection of myths, especially one belonging to a particular religious or cultural tradition.

words.ex: He hammered the nail into the wood.
words.ex_cn: 他把钉子敲进了木头里。
words.en: A nail is a thin pointed piece of metal that is hammered into materials as a fastener. It can also refer to the hard covering at the end of fingers and toes. As a verb, to nail means to fasten something with a nail or to catch or accomplish something successfully.

words.ex: The child gave a naive smile when he believed the story.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子相信这个故事时，他露出了天真的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as naïve, you think they lack experience and so expect things to be easy or people to be honest or kind.

words.ex: The child was naked in the bathtub.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在浴缸里是裸体的。
words.en: If something is naked, it is not covered by anything such as clothes or paint.

words.tr:
n. 姓名；名称；
v. 说出…的名字；命名；
words.ex: His name is Tom.
words.ex_cn: 他的名字是汤姆。
words.en: The word or words that a person, thing, or place is known by.

words.tr: adj. 无名的；匿名的；不出名的；不可名状的；
words.ex: The nameless soldier was buried with honor.
words.ex_cn: 这位无名的士兵被以荣誉安葬。
words.en: If someone or something is nameless, they do not have a name, or their name is not known.

words.ex: He has three hobbies, namely reading, swimming, and painting.
words.ex_cn: 他有三个爱好，即阅读、游泳和绘画。
words.en: You use namely to introduce detailed information about the subject you are discussing, or a particular aspect of it.

words.ex: He is the namesake of his grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他是他祖父的同名者。
words.en: A namesake is a person or thing that has the same name as another person or thing.

words.tr:
n. 小睡；打盹；
v. 小睡；打盹；
words.ex: He took a short nap after lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午饭后小睡了一会儿。
words.en: If you have a nap, you have a short sleep, usually during the day.

words.ex: He wiped his mouth with a napkin.
words.ex_cn: 他用纸巾擦了擦嘴。
words.en: A napkin is a piece of cloth or paper used at meals to protect your clothes and to wipe your mouth and fingers.

words.tr:
n. 麻醉药；镇定剂；致幻毒品
adj. 麻醉的；催眠的
words.ex: He took a narcotic for his pain.
words.ex_cn: 他服了一种麻醉药来缓解疼痛。
words.en: A narcotic is a drug that dulls the senses, relieves pain, and induces sleep. It can also refer to something that has a soothing or numbing effect.

words.tr: v. 叙述；给（电视或电影）作旁白
words.ex: He will narrate the story to his little sister.
words.ex_cn: 他将为他的小妹妹讲述这个故事。
words.en: If you narrate a story, you tell it from your own point of view.

words.ex: The narration of the story was very clear.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的叙述非常清晰。
words.en: The act or process of telling a story or describing a series of events.

words.tr:
n. 叙述；叙事；
adj. 叙述性的；
words.ex: He told a simple narrative about his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个关于他童年的简单故事。
words.en: A narrative is a story or an account of a series of events.

words.ex: The narrator told the story in a calm voice.
words.ex_cn: 叙述者用平静的声音讲述了这个故事。
words.en: A narrator is a person who tells a story, or a person who speaks during a film or television program not as an actor but to describe or discuss the pictures being shown.

words.tr:
adj. 狭窄的；窄小的；
v. 使窄小；
words.ex: The road is narrow and hard to drive on.
words.ex_cn: 这条路很窄，开车很难。
words.en: If something narrows, or if you narrow it, it becomes less wide.

words.ex: He has a nasal voice when he has a cold.
words.ex_cn: 他感冒时声音有鼻音。
words.en: Nasal is used to describe something relating to the nose or the production of sound through the nose.

words.ex: The weather today is nasty and rainy.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气令人不愉快，又阴又雨。
words.en: If you describe something as nasty, you mean it is very unpleasant, unattractive, or unkind.

words.ex: He visited his natal village for the first time.
words.ex_cn: 他第一次回到了自己的出生村庄。
words.en: Relating to the place or time of one's birth

words.ex: The nation celebrated its independence day.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家庆祝了它的独立日。
words.en: A nation is a country considered as a group of people with the same language, culture, and history, who live in a particular area under one government.

words.ex: The national flag flies high every morning.
words.ex_cn: 每天早上国旗都高高飘扬。
words.en: relating to or characteristic of a nation; common to a whole nation

words.ex: His nationality is Canadian.
words.ex_cn: 他的国籍是加拿大人。
words.en: Nationality is the legal relationship between an individual and a state, often used to refer to the country to which a person belongs.

words.tr:
adj. 本土的；
n. 土著；本地人；
words.ex: This plant is native to Australia.
words.ex_cn: 这种植物原产于澳大利亚。
words.en: A native of a particular country or region is someone who was born in that country or region.

words.ex: The children played in the natural park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在自然公园里玩耍。
words.en: Existing in or caused by nature; not made or caused by humankind.

words.tr: adv. 自然地；理所当然地；
words.ex: Babies cry naturally when they are hungry.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿饿了时会自然地哭。
words.en: in a natural manner; as a matter of course; by nature

words.ex: His nature is kind and patient.
words.ex_cn: 他的本性是善良且有耐心的。
words.en: Nature refers to the physical world and everything in it that is not made by people, including plants, animals, mountains, oceans, stars, etc. It can also refer to the basic or inherent features, character, or qualities of something.

words.ex: The naughty boy broke his mother's vase.
words.ex_cn: 那个顽皮的男孩打碎了他妈妈的花瓶。
words.en: If you say that a child is naughty, you mean that they behave badly or do not do what they are told.

words.ex: The smell of the food made her feel nausea.
words.ex_cn: 食物的气味让她感到恶心。
words.en: A feeling of sickness with an inclination to vomit.

words.ex: He works on a nautical chart.
words.ex_cn: 他正在使用一张航海图。
words.en: Nautical means relating to ships, sailing, or navigation at sea.

words.ex: He works on a naval ship.
words.ex_cn: 他在一艘军舰上工作。
words.en: Naval means relating to the navy, especially to ships that are used in war.

words.ex: The baby has a small navel.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿有一个小肚脐。
words.en: The small hollow or depression in the center of a person's belly where the umbilical cord was attached at birth.

words.tr: adj. 可航行的；适于通航的；
words.ex: The river is navigable by small boats.
words.ex_cn: 这条河可供小船航行。
words.en: If a stretch of water is navigable, it is deep and wide enough for ships to travel through.

words.ex: The ship uses GPS for navigation.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船使用GPS进行导航。
words.en: The process or activity of accurately ascertaining one's position and planning and following a route.

words.ex: He joined the navy after high school.
words.ex_cn: 他高中毕业后加入了海军。
words.en: The navy is the part of a country's armed forces that is trained to operate at sea.

words.tr:
prep. 靠近；在…附近；
adj. 近的；
adv. 近地；
words.ex: The cat is near the window.
words.ex_cn: 猫靠近窗户。
words.en: If something is near, it is not far away in distance or time.

words.tr:
adj. 附近的；
adv. 在附近；
words.ex: There is a park nearby my house.
words.ex_cn: 我家附近有一个公园。
words.en: If something is nearby, it is only a short distance away.

words.ex: I nearly missed the bus this morning.
words.ex_cn: 我今天早上差点没赶上公交车。
words.en: Almost, but not quite; very close to.

words.tr: adj. 整洁的；整齐的；有条理的
words.ex: He keeps his desk neat.
words.ex_cn: 他保持书桌整洁。
words.en: Neat things are tidy, smart, or carefully arranged.

words.ex: He doesn't necessarily agree with you.
words.ex_cn: 他并不必然同意你。
words.en: If you say that something necessarily happens or is the case, you mean that it has to happen or be the case and cannot be any different.

words.tr: adj. 必需的；必要的；必然的；
words.ex: Water is necessary for life.
words.ex_cn: 水是生命所必需的。
words.en: If something is necessary, it is needed in order for something else to happen or be done.

words.ex: The rain necessitated staying indoors.
words.ex_cn: 下雨使待在室内成为必需。
words.en: To necessitate something means to make it necessary for something to be done or to happen.

words.ex: Water is a basic necessity for life.
words.ex_cn: 水是生命的基本必需品。
words.en: Something that is necessary or indispensable.

words.ex: He hurt his neck while lifting weights.
words.ex_cn: 他在举重时伤了脖子。
words.en: The part of a person's or animal's body connecting the head to the rest of the body.

words.ex: She wears a gold necklace every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天都戴一条金项链。
words.en: A necklace is a piece of jewellery such as a chain or a string of beads which someone, usually a woman, wears around their neck.

words.tr:
v. 需要；
n. 需要；
words.ex: I need help with my homework.
words.ex_cn: 我需要帮助做作业。
words.en: If you need something, you must have it because it is essential.

words.tr: n. 必要的事物; 钱
words.ex: She used the money to buy all the needful things for the trip.
words.ex_cn: 她用这笔钱买了旅行所需的所有东西。
words.en: Necessary; required.

words.ex: She picked up a needle to sew the button.
words.ex_cn: 她拿起一根针来缝纽扣。
words.en: A needle is a thin, pointed piece of metal that is used in sewing. It has a hole at one end for thread to pass through.

words.ex: He bought a new phone, but it was needless.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一部新手机，但这是不必要的。
words.en: If you describe something as needless, you mean that it is unnecessary and often harmful or undesirable.

words.ex: The needy family received food from the charity.
words.ex_cn: 这个贫穷的家庭从慈善机构收到了食物。
words.en: Needy people do not have enough food, medicine, or clothing, or adequate houses.

words.ex: He tries to negate the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图否认事实。
words.en: If someone negates something, they say that it does not exist or is not true.

words.tr: n. 否定；反面；对立面；拒绝
words.ex: He gave a negation of the statement.
words.ex_cn: 他否定了那个陈述。
words.en: A negation is a statement that denies or contradicts another statement.

words.tr: adj. 负面的；消极的；否定的；
words.ex: The news had a negative effect on the market.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻对市场产生了负面影响。
words.en: If someone is negative or has a negative attitude, they consider only the bad aspects of a situation, rather than the good ones.

words.ex: His neglect of the project caused delays.
words.ex_cn: 他对项目的疏忽导致了延误。
words.en: If you neglect someone or something, you fail to give them the attention or care that they need.

words.ex: His negligence caused the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致了事故。
words.en: Negligence is failure to take proper care over something that you are responsible for, which might cause damage or loss.

words.tr: adj. 疏忽的；粗心的；不在意的
words.ex: He was negligent in doing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他做作业时很疏忽。
words.en: If you say that someone is negligent, you mean that they do not take enough care over something that they are responsible for.

words.ex: The error is negligible.
words.ex_cn: 这个误差可以忽略。
words.en: If you describe something as negligible, you mean that it is so small or unimportant that it is not worth considering or worrying about.

words.tr: adj. 可协商的；可转让的；可通行的
words.ex: The price is negotiable.
words.ex_cn: 价格可以商量。
words.en: If you describe something as negotiable, you mean that it can be changed or agreed upon through discussion.

words.ex: They will negotiate the price with the seller.
words.ex_cn: 他们会与卖家协商价格。
words.en: If people negotiate with each other or negotiate an agreement, they talk about a problem or a situation such as a business arrangement in order to solve the problem or complete the arrangement.

words.ex: The two sides started negotiation to solve the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 双方开始了谈判以解决冲突。
words.en: Negotiation is a discussion aimed at reaching an agreement.

words.ex: He used the word negro to describe the man, which made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他用‘黑人’这个词来描述那个男人，这让所有人都感到不舒服。
words.en: A term for a person of African descent, now considered offensive in most contexts.

words.ex: My neighbor gives me apples from her tree.
words.ex_cn: 我的邻居从她的树上给我摘苹果。
words.en: A neighbor is someone who lives near you, or a country that is next to another country.

words.tr: n. 街坊；四邻；街道；附近地区；
words.ex: I walk my dog in the neighborhood every morning.
words.ex_cn: 我每天早上在街坊遛狗。
words.en: A neighborhood is one of the parts of a town where people live.

words.ex: The neighboring house has a big garden.
words.ex_cn: 邻近的那所房子有一个大花园。
words.en: Located or living near or next to a place or person.

words.tr:
adv. 两者都不；
adj. 两者都不的；
conj. 也不；
pron. 两者都不；
words.ex: I don't like coffee, and neither do I like tea.
words.ex_cn: 我不喜欢咖啡，也不喜欢茶。
words.en: used to introduce a further negative statement after a negative one, or to indicate that a negative statement is also true of another person or thing

words.ex: My brother's son is my nephew.
words.ex_cn: 我弟弟的儿子是我的侄子。
words.en: A nephew is a son of one's sibling or sibling-in-law.

words.ex: The nerve in his finger was damaged.
words.ex_cn: 他手指里的神经受到了损伤。
words.en: A nerve is a bundle of fibers that transmits impulses of sensation to the brain or spinal cord, and impulses from these to the muscles and organs. It also refers to the courage or control needed to do something difficult or dangerous.

words.tr: adj. 紧张不安的；神经系统的；
words.ex: He felt nervous before the test.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到紧张不安。
words.en: If someone is nervous, they are frightened or worried about something that is happening or might happen, and show this in their behavior.

words.tr:
n. 窝；鸟巢；
v. 筑巢；
words.ex: The bird built a nest in the tree.
words.ex_cn: 鸟在树上筑了一个窝。
words.en: A nest is a structure made by a bird for laying eggs and sheltering its young. It can also refer to a place where insects or other animals lay eggs or raise their young. As a verb, to nest means to build or use a nest.

words.tr: v. 安顿；安居；安卧；坐落于
words.ex: The baby nestles close to her mother.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿依偎在妈妈身边。
words.en: To settle or lie comfortably within or against something.

words.tr:
adj. 净余的；
n. 网；
words.ex: The net profit after taxes is $500.
words.ex_cn: 缴税后的净收益是500美元。
words.en: A net is a piece of thin fabric or thread that is used to catch fish, insects, or other small animals. It can also refer to the amount of money remaining after all expenses have been deducted.

words.ex: The internet is a big network of computers.
words.ex_cn: 互联网是一个庞大的计算机网络。
words.en: A network is a system of lines or channels that cross or connect, or a group of broadcasting stations that connect for the simultaneous broadcast of a program.

words.tr: n. 神经症；神经衰弱症
words.ex: He has a neurosis about being late.
words.ex_cn: 他对迟到有一种神经症般的焦虑。
words.en: A neurosis is a mental illness that causes feelings of fear and worry, often leading to unreasonable behavior.

words.tr:
adj. 神经（官能）症的；神经质的；神经过敏的
n. 神经官能症患者；神经质者；神经过敏者
words.ex: She had a neurotic fear of flying.
words.ex_cn: 她对飞行有一种神经质的恐惧。
words.en: If you say that someone is neurotic, you mean that they are always worried or anxious about things that you consider unimportant.

words.ex: He stayed neutral in the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持中立。
words.en: If you say that someone is neutral, you mean that they do not support or help either side in a disagreement, competition, or war.

words.ex: He kept neutrality during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持中立。
words.en: The state of not supporting or helping either side in a conflict, disagreement, etc.; impartiality.

words.tr: v. 使中立；中和；使无效
words.ex: The government tried to neutralize the conflict by talking to both sides.
words.ex_cn: 政府试图通过与双方交谈来使冲突中立化。
words.en: To neutralize something means to stop it from having any effect or to make it ineffective.

words.ex: The neutron has no electric charge.
words.ex_cn: 中子不带电荷。
words.en: A neutron is a subatomic particle found in the nucleus of every atom except that of simple hydrogen. It has no electric charge and a mass slightly greater than that of a proton.

words.ex: He has never been to Japan.
words.ex_cn: 他从未去过日本。
words.en: At no time in the past or future; on no occasion; not ever.

words.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went for a walk.
words.ex_cn: 天下雨了；尽管如此，我们还是去散步了。
words.en: Despite what has just been said or done; nonetheless.

words.ex: He bought a new bike yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天买了一辆新自行车。
words.en: Recently made, invented, introduced, or discovered; not existing before.

words.ex: I read the news every morning.
words.ex_cn: 我每天早上看新闻。
words.en: News is information about recent events or happenings, especially as reported by newspapers, radio, television, or online media.

words.ex: He reads the newspaper every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上读报纸。
words.en: A newspaper is a publication consisting of a number of large sheets of folded paper, on which news, advertisements, and other information is printed.

words.tr:
adj. 下一个的；
adv. 随后；
pron. 下一个；
words.ex: This is the next bus to the city.
words.ex_cn: 这是下一班去城市的公交车。
words.en: Coming immediately after the present one in order, sequence, or time.

words.tr:
v. 轻咬；啃；一点点地吃
n. 一小口；轻咬；少量
words.ex: The dog nibble the biscuit slowly.
words.ex_cn: 狗慢慢地轻咬着饼干。
words.en: To nibble means to take small bites of something, especially food.

words.tr: adj. 令人愉快的；美好的；
words.ex: The weather today is nice.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气很令人愉快。
words.en: If you say that something is nice, you mean that you find it attractive, pleasant, or enjoyable.

words.tr: n. 准确；精确；细节；细微的差别
words.ex: The nicety of the measurement surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个测量的准确性让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A nicety is a fine detail or distinction, especially one that is considered to be important or elegant.

words.ex: The coin is made of nickel.
words.ex_cn: 这枚硬币是镍制的。
